title.en: Volume 99 Biographies 24: Li Gang, Li Daliang Family Descendent: Jiongxiu, Dai Zhouzhi: Zhide, Liu Ji, Cui Renshi and Grandson: Shi
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第二十四 李綱 李大亮族孫:迥秀 戴冑侄:至德 劉洎 崔仁師孫:湜 Volume 99 Biographies 24: Li Gang, Li Daliang Family Descendent: Jiongxiu, Dai Zhouzhi: Zhide, Liu Ji, Cui Renshi and Grandson: Shi

sentences.zh: 李綱孫:安仁 安靜 李大亮兄子:道裕 族孫:迥秀 戴冑侄:至德 劉洎附:樂彥瑋 崔仁師孫:湜 液 澄

translations.literal: Li Gang — grandsons: Anren and Anjing. Li Daliang — elder brother's son: Daoyu; clansman grandson: Jiongxiu. Dai Zhou — nephew: Zhide. Liu Ji, with appended [biography of] Yue Yanwei. Cui Renshi — grandsons: Shi, Ye, and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang (grandsons Anren and Anjing); Li Daliang (elder brother's son Daoyu, clansman grandson Jiongxiu); Dai Zhou (nephew Zhide); Liu Ji (with Yue Yanwei appended); Cui Renshi (grandsons Shi, Ye, and Cheng).

sentences.zh: 李綱，字文紀，觀州蓚人。

translations.literal: Li Gang, styled Wénjì, was a man of Liao in Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang, courtesy name Wénjì, came from Liao in Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，尚風節。

translations.literal: In youth he was open-handed and magnanimous, and he honored integrity and principle.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was generous and high-minded, and he prized moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 始名瑗，慕張綱為人，改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuán; admiring Zhang Gang's character, he changed it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Yuán; admiring Zhang Gang's conduct, he took Gang as his name.

sentences.zh: 仕周為齊王憲參軍事。

translations.literal: He served the Northern Zhou as an aide on the staff of Prince Xian of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Zhou he served on the staff of Prince Xian of Qi.

sentences.zh: 宣帝將殺憲，召僚屬誣左其罪，綱矢死無橈辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to kill Xian, he summoned the staff to falsely assign blame to him; Gang swore he would die rather than yield a bending word.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan prepared to execute Xian, he called in the staff to fabricate charges against him; Gang vowed he would die before he would speak a crooked word.

sentences.zh: 及憲誅，露車載屍，故吏奔匿，綱撫棺號慟，為瘞訖，乃去。

translations.literal: When Xian was executed, his corpse was carried on an open cart; former subordinates fled and hid, but Gang stroked the coffin and wailed aloud, buried him to completion, and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xian was put to death, his body was hauled on an open cart; former officials scattered in hiding, but Gang clung to the coffin and cried out in grief, saw to his burial, and only then left.

sentences.zh: 事隋為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he held the post of Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子勇宴宮臣，左庶子唐令則奏琵琶，又歌《武媚娘曲》。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong entertained palace officials; the Left Vice Director Tang Lingze played the pipa and also sang the tune "Lady Wu Mei."
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yong feasted his palace officials, the Left Vice Director Tang Lingze played the pipa and sang "The Song of Lady Wu Mei."

sentences.zh: 綱曰：「令則官調護，乃自比倡優，進淫聲，惑視聽，誠使上聞之，豈不為殿下累乎？

translations.literal: Gang said: "Lingze's office is to harmonize and protect, yet he compares himself to entertainers, presents licentious sounds, and misleads eyes and ears—if the sovereign should hear of this, would it not become a burden upon Your Highness?"
translations.idiomatic: Gang said, "Lingze's duty is to guide and protect you, yet he acts like a performer, offers lewd music, and corrupts what people see and hear—if the emperor learns of this, will it not reflect badly on you, Your Highness?"

sentences.zh: 臣請正其罪。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that his crime be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be punished for this offense.

sentences.zh: 」勇曰：「置之，我欲為樂耳！

translations.literal: " Yong said: "Let it be—I only want my pleasure!"
translations.idiomatic: " Yong replied, "Leave it—I only want my amusement!"

sentences.zh: 」後勇廢，文帝切讓，官屬無敢對，綱獨曰：「陛下不素教，故太子至此。

translations.literal: " Later Yong was deposed; Emperor Wen sharply reproached [the staff], and none of the officials dared reply—only Gang said: "Your Majesty has not consistently instructed him, and so the Heir Apparent has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: " After Yong was deposed, Emperor Wen sternly rebuked the staff, and no one dared answer except Gang, who said, "Your Majesty never taught him consistently, and that is why the crown prince has come to this pass."

sentences.zh: 太子資中人，得賢者輔而善，得不肖導而惡，奈何歌舞鷹犬纖兒使日侍側？

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent's native endowment is middling among men: with worthy men to assist him he becomes good, with unworthy men to guide him he becomes bad—why allow singers, dancers, hawks, dogs, and petty youths to attend him daily at his side?
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is an ordinary man by nature: with worthy advisers he improves, with unworthy ones he goes astray—so why let singers, dancers, hunting birds and dogs, and frivolous companions wait on him day after day?

sentences.zh: 何特太子罪邪？

translations.literal: Why lay the blame on the Heir Apparent alone?
translations.idiomatic: Why blame the crown prince alone?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「以汝為洗馬，何不擇人？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I made you Mentor—why did you not choose [better] men?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I appointed you his mentor—why did you not choose better companions for him?"

sentences.zh: 」綱曰：「臣非東宮得言者。

translations.literal: " Gang said: "Your servant was not one who could speak freely in the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: " Gang replied, "I was not someone the Eastern Palace would heed."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕過矣！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The fault is mine!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The fault is mine!"

sentences.zh: 」擢尚書右丞。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時楊素、蘇威用事，綱據正不詭迎隨，素等多憾。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Su and Su Wei held power; Gang held to what was right and would not bend or flatter to follow them, and Su and the others bore much resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and Su Wei were then in control of affairs; Gang stood on principle and would neither bend nor court them, and they came to resent him deeply.

sentences.zh: 會大將軍劉方討林邑，素言林邑多珍貲，非綱不可任，遂署行軍司馬。

translations.literal: It happened that the Great General Liu Fang was campaigning against Linyi; Su said Linyi held many precious goods and that none but Gang could be entrusted with the task, and so Gang was appointed army campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the great general Liu Fang marched against Linyi, Su claimed the region was rich in treasure and that only Gang was fit for the assignment, and Gang was made campaign marshal on the expedition.

sentences.zh: 方揣素指，數危辱之，幾殆。

translations.literal: Fang divined Su's intent and repeatedly put him in peril and humiliated him, so that he nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Fang understood what Su wanted and repeatedly threatened and humiliated him, nearly bringing about his death.

sentences.zh: 軍還，不得調。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he received no transfer or promotion.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was given no new appointment.

sentences.zh: 稍除齊王府司馬。

translations.literal: After a time he was appointed Vice Commander of the Prince of Qi's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually made vice commander on the staff of the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 復詔出南海，應接林邑。

translations.literal: He was again ordered out to the Southern Sea to receive and deal with Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered south to the coast to handle relations with Linyi.

sentences.zh: 久不召，乃身入奏。

translations.literal: For a long time he was not summoned back, so he went in person to present a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When he was not recalled for a long time, he went to the capital in person to report.

sentences.zh: 威劾綱擅去所部，以屬吏。

translations.literal: Su impeached Gang for leaving his post without authorization and handed him over to the local officials for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Su charged Gang with abandoning his jurisdiction without leave and turned him over to local authorities.

sentences.zh: 會赦免，屏居鄠。

translations.literal: An amnesty intervened and he was pardoned; he withdrew to live in seclusion at E.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared by a general amnesty and lived in retirement at E.

sentences.zh: 大業末，賊帥何潘仁劫為長史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign, the bandit chief He Panren seized him and forced him to serve as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era, the rebel leader He Panren took him captive and compelled him to serve as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 高祖平京師，綱上謁，授丞相府司錄參軍，封新昌縣公，領選舉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu pacified the capital, Gang came to pay his respects; he was appointed Registrar of the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed as Duke of Xinchang, and put in charge of selection and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took Chang'an, Gang presented himself and was made registrar in the chancellor's office, enfeoffed as Duke of Xinchang, and placed in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 受禪，拜禮部尚書兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: When the throne was received [by abdication], he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu accepted the abdication, Gang was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrently steward of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉為并州總管，縱左右攘奪，民愁苦，宇文歆諫，不聽，騰狀顯言，王坐免。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yuánjí served as regional commander of Bingzhou and let his attendants seize and plunder at will, so the people were in distress; Yuwen Xin remonstrated but was not heeded, and sent up a memorial stating the facts plainly; the prince was removed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuánjí of Qi was regional commander at Bingzhou and allowed his followers to loot freely, bringing the people to misery; Yuwen Xin remonstrated in vain and then submitted an open memorial; the prince was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 俄而復留，下危惴。

translations.literal: Before long he was kept on again, and those below lived in fear and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was kept in the post again, and his subordinates were left in dread.

sentences.zh: 劉武周入太原，元吉懼，棄軍奔京師，并州陷。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou entered Taiyuan, Yuánjí was afraid, abandoned the army, and fled to the capital; Bingzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou took Taiyuan, Yuánjí panicked, abandoned his troops, and fled to the capital, and Bingzhou was lost.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謂綱曰：「王年少，不習事，故以歆及竇誕佐之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and said to Gang: "The prince is young and unversed in affairs, which is why I set Xin and Dou Yan to assist him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and told Gang, "The prince is young and inexperienced, which is why I assigned Xin and Dou Yan to assist him."

sentences.zh: 太原，興王地，兵十萬，粟支十年，奈何一旦棄去？

translations.literal: Taiyuan is the land where kings rise: a hundred thousand troops, grain enough for ten years—how could it be abandoned in a single day?
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is where dynasties are founded—there were a hundred thousand troops and grain for ten years—how could it be thrown away overnight?

sentences.zh: 歆建此計，我當斬於軍。

translations.literal: Xin devised this plan—I ought to execute him before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xin devised this plan; I should have him beheaded before the troops.

sentences.zh: 」綱曰：「王過惡，誕養成之。

translations.literal: " Gang said: "The prince's faults and evils were nurtured and brought to completion by Yan."
translations.idiomatic: " Gang said, "The prince's misconduct was fostered by Yan."

sentences.zh: 歆事王淺，有闕必諍。

translations.literal: Xin's service to the prince was brief, but whenever there was a fault he was sure to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had served the prince only a short time, yet whenever he saw a fault he spoke up.

sentences.zh: 今賴歆計，使陛下不失愛子，且有功，又可加罪乎？

translations.literal: Now, thanks to Xin's plan, Your Majesty has not lost a beloved son, and he even has merit—how can punishment be added on top of that?
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Xin's counsel you have not lost a beloved son, and he even deserves credit—how can you punish him for that?

sentences.zh: 」翼日，帝悟，引綱升禦榻，勞曰：「卿不言，我幾濫罰。

translations.literal: " The next day the emperor understood, drew Gang up onto the imperial couch, and said in consolation: "Had you not spoken, I would nearly have punished wrongly."
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the emperor saw his error, drew Gang onto the imperial couch, and said, "Had you not spoken, I would almost have punished the wrong man."

sentences.zh: 」於是釋歆，然猶貸誕也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xin was released, but Yan was still spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin was released, though Yan was still let off.

sentences.zh: 帝以舞工安叱奴為散騎常侍，綱諫曰：「周家均工樂胥不得預士伍，雖復妙如師襄，才如子野，皆繼世不易業。

translations.literal: The emperor made the dancer An Chinu a Regular Attendant; Gang remonstrated, saying: "Under the Zhou, workers in equal measure and music officials were not allowed among the ranks of gentlemen; even if one were as skilled as Master Xiang or as talented as Ziye, each inherited his trade and did not change his occupation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed the dancer An Chinu Regular Attendant; Gang objected: "In Zhou times, artisans and music officials were barred from the warrior and scholar ranks—even men as gifted as Master Xiang or Ziye inherited their craft and did not change their calling."

sentences.zh: 故魏武使禰衡擊鼓，衡先解朝衣，曰：'不敢以先王法服為伶人衣。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Wu of Wei had Mi Heng beat the drum; Heng first removed his court robes and said, 'I dare not let the ritual garments of former kings serve as a performer's dress.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why Cao Cao had Mi Heng beat the drum—Heng first stripped off his court robes and said he would not wear the ritual dress of former kings as a performer's costume.

sentences.zh: '齊高緯封曹妙達為王，以安馬駒開府，有國家者，可為鑒戒。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Gao of Northern Qi enfeoffed Cao Miaoda as a prince and made An Maju Grand Marshal of the Vanguard—rulers of states may take this as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei of Northern Qi made Cao Miaoda a prince and gave An Maju an honorary commandery—anyone who holds a state should take that as a warning.

sentences.zh: 今新造天下，開太平之基，功臣賞未及遍，高才猶伏草茅，而先令舞胡鳴玉曳組，位五品，趨丹地，殆非創業垂統、貽子孫之道也。

translations.literal: Now, having newly forged the realm and laid the foundation of great peace, rewards to meritorious servants have not yet reached all, and men of high talent still lie hidden in thatched cottages—yet you first let a dancing barbarian jingle jade and trail ribbons, grant him fifth rank, and hurry into the scarlet court: this is scarcely the way to found an enterprise, hand down a tradition, and bequeath a legacy to one's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: You have only just won the empire and begun the foundations of peace; meritorious men are not yet fully rewarded and able talent still waits in obscurity—yet a dancing foreigner is given jade pendants and official ribbons, fifth rank, and access to the scarlet hall. That is hardly how to build a dynasty and leave a worthy example to your heirs.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not accept [the advice].
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 綱在東宮，太子建成尤加禮，嘗游溫湯，綱疾不從。

translations.literal: Gang was in the Eastern Palace; Crown Prince Jiancheng treated him with especial courtesy; once when the prince visited the hot springs, Gang was ill and did not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: While Gang served in the Eastern Palace, Crown Prince Jiancheng treated him with particular respect; on one visit to the hot springs the prince went without him because Gang was ill.

sentences.zh: 有進魚者，太子使膾之，唐儉、趙元楷自言其能。

translations.literal: Someone presented fish; the prince had it sliced raw, and Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai each claimed the skill to do it.
translations.idiomatic: When fish was brought in, the prince had it prepared as sashimi, and Tang Jian and Zhao Yuankai each boasted of his skill at the task.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「操刀膾鯉和鼎味，公等善之。

translations.literal: The prince said: "Wielding the knife to slice carp and harmonize the flavor of the tripod—you gentlemen are skilled at that."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "You are adept at wielding the knife, slicing carp, and seasoning the cauldron."

sentences.zh: 若弼諧審諭，固屬綱矣。

translations.literal: If it is assisting and harmonizing and examining and instructing, that surely belongs to Gang."
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to assisting and guiding policy, that is Gang's province."

sentences.zh: 」遣使賜絹二百匹。

translations.literal: " He sent a messenger to bestow two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent a messenger with two hundred bolts of silk as a gift.

sentences.zh: 後太子浸狎亡賴，猜間朝廷，綱頻諫不見聽，遂乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Later the prince grew increasingly intimate with worthless men and suspicious of the court; Gang remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded, and he therefore asked to retire on account of old bones.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince grew closer to ruffians and more suspicious of the court; Gang remonstrated again and again without being heard and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝罵曰：「卿為潘仁長史，而羞朕尚書邪？

translations.literal: The emperor scolded him, saying: "You served as chief clerk to Panren—are you ashamed of being my Minister?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor berated him: "You were chief clerk to Panren—are you too proud to remain my minister?"

sentences.zh: 」綱頓首曰：「潘仁，賊也，志殘殺，然每諫輒止，為其長史，故無愧。

translations.literal: " Gang bowed his head and said: "Panren was a bandit, bent on slaughter, yet whenever I remonstrated he would stop—serving as his chief clerk, I therefore have no shame."
translations.idiomatic: " Gang kowtowed and said, "Panren was a rebel bent on killing, yet he stopped whenever I remonstrated; as his chief clerk I have nothing to be ashamed of."

sentences.zh: 陛下功成，厚自伐，臣言如持水內石，敢久為尚書乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty's achievement is complete, yet you greatly boast of yourself; my words are like holding water inside stone—how dare I long remain Minister?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's success is won, yet you congratulate yourself lavishly; my words are like pouring water on stone—how can I remain minister for long?

sentences.zh: 且臣事東宮，東宮又與臣忤，是以上印綬。

translations.literal: Moreover, I serve the Eastern Palace, and the Eastern Palace is again at odds with me—therefore I return my seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I serve the Eastern Palace, and the crown prince is at odds with me—that is why I am returning my seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 」帝謝曰：「知公直士，幸卒輔吾兒。

translations.literal: " The emperor apologized, saying: "I know you are an upright man; I hope you will in the end continue to assist my son."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor apologized: "I know you are an honest man; please stay and help my son to the end."

sentences.zh: 」乃拜太子少保，尚書、詹事如故。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retaining his posts as Minister and Steward.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent while keeping his posts as minister and steward.

sentences.zh: 綱上書太子曰：「綱老矣，幸未就木，備位保傅，冀得效愚鄙。

translations.literal: Gang wrote to the prince: "Gang is old; fortunately he has not yet entered the coffin wood. Holding a place among the guardians and tutors, he hopes to offer his humble foolishness."
translations.idiomatic: Gang wrote to the prince: "I am old, and fortunate not yet to be in my coffin. In my post as your guardian I hope to offer what little wisdom I have."

sentences.zh: 日殿下飲酒過量，非養生之道。

translations.literal: Daily Your Highness drinks to excess—this is not the way to nurture life.
translations.idiomatic: You drink too much each day, which is no way to preserve your health.

sentences.zh: 凡為人子，務孝謹，以慰上心，不宜聽受邪說，與朝廷生槊間。

translations.literal: As a rule, one who is a son should devote himself to filial piety and prudence to comfort the heart above; he should not heed perverse doctrines and breed estrangement with the court.
translations.idiomatic: As a son you should be filial and careful to comfort your father; you must not listen to wicked counsel and breed estrangement with the court.

sentences.zh: 」太子覽書不懌，所為益縱。

translations.literal: " The prince read the letter and was displeased; his conduct grew ever more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince read the letter with displeasure and behaved even more recklessly.

sentences.zh: 綱悒悒不自賴，固請老，優詔解尚書。

translations.literal: Gang was depressed and could not rely on himself; he firmly asked to retire on account of age, and an excellent edict released him from the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Gang grew despondent and could no longer bear the post; he pressed to retire, and an edict graciously relieved him of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 帝以綱隋名臣，手敕未嘗名。

translations.literal: Because Gang was a famous minister of the Sui, in the emperor's own hand-written edicts he was never addressed by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gang was a renowned minister of the Sui, the emperor never used his personal name in handwritten edicts.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，復為少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was again made Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was again appointed Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 以足疾賜步輿，聽乘至閤，問以政事。

translations.literal: Because of illness in his feet he was granted a carrying chair and permitted to ride as far as the gate, and was questioned on affairs of government.
translations.idiomatic: Because of a foot ailment he was given a sedan chair and allowed to ride to the palace gate, where the emperor consulted him on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 詣東宮，太子承乾為拜，每聽政，必詔綱與房玄齡、王珪侍坐。

translations.literal: When he went to the Eastern Palace, Crown Prince Chengan performed a bow for him; whenever the prince held audience, Gang was always ordered to sit in attendance with Fang Xuanling and Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited the Eastern Palace, Crown Prince Chengan bowed to him; whenever the prince held court, Gang was always summoned to sit with Fang Xuanling and Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 嘗言曰：「托六尺之孤，寄百里之命，古人為難，綱以為易！

translations.literal: He once said: "Entrusting a child not yet six feet tall and committing the fate of a hundred-li state—the ancients found this hard; Gang finds it easy!"
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Entrusting an orphan not yet full grown and the fate of the realm—the ancients found that hard, but I find it easy!"

sentences.zh: 」故發言陳事，毅然不可奪。

translations.literal: " Therefore when he spoke and laid out affairs, he was resolute and could not be turned aside.
translations.idiomatic: " So when he spoke on public matters, he was firm and could not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 及疾，帝遣玄齡至家存問。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, the emperor sent Xuanling to his home to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, the emperor sent Fang Xuanling to his home to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年八十五，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰貞，太子為立碑。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged eighty-five; he was posthumously granted Grand Marshal of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, given the posthumous title Zhen, and the crown prince erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at eighty-five; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal of the Palace with Three Excellencies honors, given the posthumous name Zhen, and the crown prince erected a stele in his memory.

sentences.zh: 初，齊王憲女嫠居，綱厚恤之。

translations.literal: Earlier, a daughter of Prince Xian of Qi lived as a widow; Gang treated her with generous care.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a widowed daughter of Prince Xian of Qi had lived in hardship; Gang had supported her generously.

sentences.zh: 及卒，女被髮號哭，如喪其親然。

translations.literal: When he died, the woman let down her hair and wailed aloud, as though mourning her own parent.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, she let down her hair and wailed as if she had lost a parent.

sentences.zh: 綱在隋，宦不進，筮之得《鼎》。

translations.literal: While Gang was under the Sui his official career did not advance; he divined and obtained the hexagram Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui, Gang's official career stalled; when he divined, he received the hexagram Ding (The Cauldron).

sentences.zh: 筮人曰：「君當為卿輔，然待易姓乃如志。

translations.literal: The diviner said: "You are destined to become a minister and aide, but you must wait until the surname changes before your wish is fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said, "You are destined to serve as a chief minister, but you must wait until the dynasty changes before your wish is fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 仕不知退，折足為敗。

translations.literal: In office, not knowing when to withdraw—a broken foot means defeat."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not know when to retire from office, a broken foot will be your downfall."

sentences.zh: 」故綱雖顯于唐，數稱疾辭位云。

translations.literal: " Therefore, although Gang was eminent in Tang, he repeatedly pleaded illness to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: " That is why, though eminent under Tang, Gang repeatedly pleaded illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 孫安仁、安靜。

translations.literal: His grandsons were Anren and Anjing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Anren and Anjing.

sentences.zh: 孫 安仁

translations.literal: Grandson Anren
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Anren

sentences.zh: 安仁，永徽中為太子左庶子，太子忠廢還邸，寮屬奔散，獨安仁泣拜而去。

translations.literal: Anren, in the Yonghui era, served as Left Vice Director of the Heir Apparent; when Crown Prince Zhong was deposed and returned to his residence, the staff scattered in flight—only Anren wept, bowed, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During Yonghui, Anren served as left vice director of the crown prince; when Prince Zhong was deposed and sent back to his residence, the staff fled—only Anren wept, bowed, and left.

sentences.zh: 終恒州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 孫 安靜

translations.literal: Grandson Anjing
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Anjing

sentences.zh: 安靜，天授中為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Anjing, in the Tianshou era, served as General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianshou, Anjing served as general of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 武氏革命，群臣皆勸進，安靜獨無所請。

translations.literal: When the Wu clan carried out the dynastic change, all the ministers urged her to take the throne; Anjing alone made no petition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wu clan seized the throne, the courtiers all urged her to ascend; Anjing alone made no petition.

sentences.zh: 及收系獄，來俊臣問狀，安靜曰：「正以我唐舊臣，殺之可也。

translations.literal: When he was seized and imprisoned, Lai Junchen questioned him; Anjing said: "It is precisely because I am an old minister of Tang that you may kill me."
translations.idiomatic: When he was arrested and imprisoned, Lai Junchen interrogated him; Anjing said, "Kill me precisely because I am an old minister of Tang."

sentences.zh: 若詰其狀，吾誰欺？

translations.literal: If you press the charges, whom would I deceive?
translations.idiomatic: If you press charges against me, whom would I deceive?

sentences.zh: 」俊臣誣殺之。

translations.literal: " Junchen falsely charged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Junchen framed him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，錄忠臣後，訪子孫已絕，乃贈安靜太子少師。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era, when recording the descendants of loyal ministers, they found Anjing's line had died out, and so posthumously granted Anjing the title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang, when the court recorded descendants of loyal ministers, it found Anjing had no heirs left and posthumously granted him the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 自綱五世同居，安仁、安靜復以義烈聞，世稱李氏不衰。

translations.literal: From Gang onward five generations lived together under one roof; Anren and Anjing were again famed for righteousness and fierce loyalty, and the age said the Li clan did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: From Gang's time five generations of the family had lived together; Anren and Anjing won further renown for righteousness and loyalty, and people said the Li line would never fade.

sentences.zh: 李大亮

translations.literal: Li Daliang
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang

sentences.zh: 李大亮，京兆涇陽人。

translations.literal: Li Daliang was a man of Jingyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang came from Jingyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖琰，為魏度支尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan served as Minister of Revenue for Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had been Minister of Revenue under Wei.

sentences.zh: 大亮有文武才略，隋末，署龐玉行軍兵曹。

translations.literal: Daliang possessed both civil and military talent and strategy; at the end of the Sui he was appointed army clerk on Pang Yu's campaign staff.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang had both literary and military gifts; at the end of the Sui he served on Pang Yu's campaign staff as army clerk.

sentences.zh: 李密寇東都，玉戰敗，大亮被禽。

translations.literal: When Li Mi raided the Eastern Capital, Yu was defeated in battle and Daliang was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi attacked the Eastern Capital, Pang Yu was defeated and Daliang was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 賊將張弼異之，就執百餘人皆死，獨釋大亮，引與語，遂定交。

translations.literal: The rebel general Zhang Bi thought him remarkable; of more than a hundred prisoners taken at once, all were put to death—only Daliang was released; Bi drew him into conversation, and they formed a bond of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Zhang Bi was struck by him; of more than a hundred captives taken together, all were killed except Daliang, whom Bi released; they talked and became friends.

sentences.zh: 高祖入關，大亮自歸，授土門令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu entered the passes, Daliang came over of his own accord and was appointed magistrate of Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes, Daliang submitted and was appointed magistrate of Tumen.

sentences.zh: 方歲饑，境多盜賊。

translations.literal: Just then there was famine in the year, and within the district there were many bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had struck the region, and bandits were numerous in the district.

sentences.zh: 大亮招亡散，撫貧瘠，賣所乘馬，稍稍資業之，勸墾田，歲大熟。

translations.literal: Daliang gathered the scattered who had fled, comforted the poor and weak, sold the horse he rode, gradually supplied them with means to make a living, urged them to open wasteland for planting, and that year the harvest was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang gathered refugees, comforted the destitute, sold his own horse to help them gradually establish livelihoods, urged them to reclaim farmland, and that year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 間出擊盜，所至輒平。

translations.literal: From time to time he went out to strike at bandits; wherever he went he at once pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He also led raids against bandits and pacified every place he reached.

sentences.zh: 秦王行北境，下書獎勞，賜馬五乘，帛五十段。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin toured the northern frontier, he issued a letter commending and consoling [Daliang], bestowing five teams of horses and fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin toured the northern frontier, he sent a letter of commendation and rewarded Daliang with five teams of horses and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 頃之，胡賊大至，大亮度不能拒，乃單馬詣營說豪帥，為分別禍福，賊眾感服，遂相率降。

translations.literal: Before long barbarian bandits arrived in great force; Daliang estimated he could not resist, so he went alone on horseback to their camp to persuade the chieftains, distinguishing for them fortune and misfortune; the band felt moved and submitted, and thereupon followed one another in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon barbarian raiders came in force; seeing he could not hold them off, Daliang rode alone to their camp, explained the consequences to the chiefs, and won them over so that they surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 大亮殺所乘馬與之食，至步而返。

translations.literal: Daliang killed the horse he rode and gave it to them for food, then returned on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered his own horse to feed them and walked home.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之悅，擢金州總管府司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was pleased, promoting him to campaign marshal of the Jinzhou regional headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to campaign marshal at Jinzhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 王弘烈據襄陽，詔大亮安撫樊、鄧，因圖之，進擊，下十餘城。

translations.literal: Wang Honglie held Xiangyang; an edict ordered Daliang to pacify Fan and Deng, and thereby scheme against him; advancing to attack, he took more than ten cities.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Honglie held Xiangyang; Daliang was ordered to pacify Fan and Deng and take him on, advancing to capture more than ten cities.

sentences.zh: 遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 復使徇廣州，至九江，會輔公祏反，以計禽其將張善安。

translations.literal: He was again sent to campaign toward Guangzhou; reaching Jiujiang, he encountered Fu Gongshi's rebellion and by stratagem captured his general Zhang Shan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent again toward Guangzhou; at Jiujiang he met Fu Gongshi's rebellion and by strategy captured his general Zhang Shan'an.

sentences.zh: 公祏方圍猷州，刺史左難當固守，大亮率兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Gongshi was then besieging Youzhou; the prefect Zuo Nandang held firm in defense, and Daliang led troops to strike and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi was besieging Youzhou while Prefect Zuo Nandang held out; Daliang led troops and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 遷越州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regional commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，徙交州，封武陽縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was moved to Jiaozhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was posted to Jiaozhou and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 召授太府卿，復出涼州都督。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury, then again sent out as regional commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury, then sent out again as regional commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗有台使見名鷹，諷大亮獻之。

translations.literal: Once an emissary from the central government saw a famous hawk and hinted that Daliang should present it.
translations.idiomatic: Once a capital envoy saw a prized hawk and hinted that Daliang should present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 大亮密表曰：「陛下絕畋獵久矣，而使者求鷹。

translations.literal: Daliang submitted a secret memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has long since renounced hunting, yet the envoy seeks a hawk."
translations.idiomatic: Daliang wrote a secret memorial: "Your Majesty has long renounced the hunt, yet this envoy asks for a hawk."

sentences.zh: 信陛下意邪，乃乖昔旨；

translations.literal: If one trusts Your Majesty's intent, this contradicts your former purpose;
translations.idiomatic: If we trust your intent, this contradicts your former policy;

sentences.zh: 如其擅求，是使非其才。

translations.literal: if he sought it on his own authority, that would show he was not fit for his post."
translations.idiomatic: if he sought it on his own, that would show he is unfit for his post."

sentences.zh: 」太宗報書曰：「有臣如此，朕何憂！

translations.literal: " Emperor Taizong replied in writing: "With a minister such as this, what have I to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong wrote back: "With a minister like you, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 古人以一言之重訂千金，今賜胡瓶一，雖亡千鎰，乃朕所自禦。

translations.literal: The ancients valued a single word at a thousand in gold; now I bestow one barbarian flask—though it is not worth a thousand yi, it is what I myself have used.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients held a single word worth a thousand in gold; I send you one foreign flask—not worth a thousand yi, but something I have used myself.

sentences.zh: 」又賜荀悅《漢紀》，曰：「悅論議深博，極為政之體，公宜繹味之。

translations.literal: " He also gave him Xun Yue's Hanji, saying: "Yue's discussions are profound and broad, reaching to the very substance of government—you should ponder and savor them."
translations.idiomatic: " He also gave him Xun Yue's Hanji, saying, "Yue's arguments are deep and broad and get to the heart of governance—you should study them carefully."

sentences.zh: 」時突厥亡，帝遂欲懷四夷，諸部降者，人賜袍一領、帛五匹，首領拜將軍、中郎將，列五品者贏百員。

translations.literal: " At that time the Turks had perished, and the emperor wished to win over the four barbarians; to each tribesman who submitted he gave one robe and five bolts of silk, and to chieftains he granted the titles of general and gentleman-cadet—those ranked at the fifth grade exceeded a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: " The Turks had fallen, and the emperor sought to win over the frontier peoples; each tribesman who submitted received a robe and five bolts of silk, chiefs were made generals or gentleman-cadets, and fifth-rank appointments exceeded a hundred.

sentences.zh: 又置降胡河南。

translations.literal: He also settled surrendered barbarians south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered barbarians were also settled south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 詔大亮為西北道安撫大使，使以綏大度設、拓設、泥熟特勒及七姓種落之未附者，峙糧磧口賑其饑。

translations.literal: An edict made Daliang Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, charging him to soothe Dadu She, Tuo She, the Nishu Tegin, and the seven-surname tribes not yet attached, and to station grain at Qikou to relieve their famine.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang was made Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit to win over Dadu She, Tuo She, the Nishu Tegin, and unaffiliated tribes of the seven surnames, and to stock grain at Qikou to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 大亮上言：「臣聞欲綏遠者必自近。

translations.literal: Daliang submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that those who wish to pacify the distant must begin with what is near."
translations.idiomatic: Daliang memorialized: "I have heard that to pacify distant peoples one must begin at home."

sentences.zh: 中國，天下本根，四夷猶枝葉也。

translations.literal: The Central Realm is the root of all under Heaven; the four barbarians are but branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: China is the root of the empire; the four barbarians are but branches and leaves.

sentences.zh: 殘本根，厚枝葉，而曰求安，未之有也。

translations.literal: To injure the root yet thicken the branches and leaves, and then speak of seeking security—never has such a thing existed.
translations.idiomatic: To wound the root while fattening the branches and then expect security has never worked.

sentences.zh: 屬者突厥傾國入朝，陛下不即俘江淮變其俗，而加賜物帛，悉官之，引處內地，豈久安計哉？

translations.literal: Recently the Turks came to court with their whole nation; Your Majesty did not at once detain them on the Jiang-Huai and change their customs, but instead added gifts of goods and silk, made them all officials, and settled them within the interior—how can this be a plan for lasting peace?
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks came to court with their whole people, Your Majesty did not detain them on the Jiang-Huai to change their ways, but lavished gifts, made them all officials, and settled them inland—is that a plan for lasting peace?

sentences.zh: 今伊吾雖臣，遠在荒鹵。

translations.literal: Now Yiwu, though it submits, lies far off in wild salt wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu may submit, but it lies far off in the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 臣以為諸稱籓請附者，宜羈縻受之，使居塞外，畏威懷德，永為籓臣。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that all who call themselves vassals and ask to attach should be received under loose control, made to dwell beyond the passes, in awe of majesty and cherishing virtue, forever vassal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I believe those who declare themselves vassals should be received under loose control, kept beyond the frontier, awed by your might and drawn by your virtue, and kept forever as tributaries.

sentences.zh: 謂之荒服者，故臣而不內，所謂行虛惠，收實福。

translations.literal: What is called the distant service is therefore to have them submit as ministers but not bring them within—this is what is meant by offering empty favor and reaping real blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The distant service means they submit as vassals but are not brought inside—offering nominal favor while gaining real benefit.

sentences.zh: 河西積困夷狄，州縣蕭條，加因隋亂，殘耗已甚。

translations.literal: Hexi had long been worn down by barbarians; prefectures and counties were desolate, and on top of this came the disorders of Sui, so the waste and depletion were already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi had long suffered from barbarian raids; districts were desolate, and Sui's disorders had left the region badly depleted.

sentences.zh: 臣愚願停招慰，省勞役，使邊人得就農畮，此中國利也。

translations.literal: Your servant, in his foolishness, wishes to halt recruitment and consolation, reduce corvée labor, and let the people of the frontier return to farming—this would benefit the Central Realm.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we stop recruiting and reassuring them, lighten labor service, and let frontier people farm again—that would benefit China.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其計。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 八年，為劍南道巡省大使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he served as touring inspector commissioner of the Jiannan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as touring inspector of the Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會討吐谷渾，為河東道行軍總管，與李靖俱出北道，涉青海，觀河源，與虜遇蜀渾山，大戰，破之，俘其名王，獲雜畜數萬，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When a campaign was mounted against Tuyuhun, he served as campaign commander of the Hedong Circuit; with Li Jing he both advanced by the northern route, crossed Qinghai, viewed the source of the Yellow River, met the enemy at Shuhun Mountain, fought a great battle, defeated them, captured their famous kings, took tens of thousands of mixed livestock, and was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Tuyuhun he was campaign commander on the Hedong route; with Li Jing he marched north, crossed Qinghai, saw the Yellow River's source, met the enemy at Shuhun Mountain, routed them, captured their princes and tens of thousands of livestock, and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Great General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed great general of the Right Guards.

sentences.zh: 晉王為皇太子，詔大亮兼右衛率，又兼工部尚書，身三職，宿衛兩宮。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, an edict made Daliang concurrently commander of the Right Guards, and also concurrent Minister of Works—holding three offices in person, he guarded both palaces by night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Daliang was made concurrently commander of the Right Guards and Minister of Works—three posts at once—guarding both palaces.

sentences.zh: 每番直，常假寐。

translations.literal: On each watch rotation he would often doze.
translations.idiomatic: On each watch he would often doze.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「公在，我得酣臥。」

translations.literal: The emperor said in consolation: "With you here, I can sleep soundly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With you on duty, I can sleep in peace."

sentences.zh: 十八年，幸洛陽，詔副房玄齡居守。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year [the emperor] visited Luoyang and ordered Daliang to assist Fang Xuanling in remaining to guard [the capital].
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the emperor went to Luoyang and left Daliang with Fang Xuanling to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄齡稱「有王陵、周勃節，可倚大事」。

translations.literal: Xuanling said of him: "He has the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and can be relied on for great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling said he had the steadfastness of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and could be trusted with grave matters.

sentences.zh: 俄寢疾，帝親和藥，驛賜之。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill in bed; the emperor personally mixed medicine and sent it by post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill; the emperor mixed medicine himself and sent it by courier.

sentences.zh: 臨終，表請罷遼東役；

translations.literal: At the point of death he memorialized asking that the Liaodong corvée be halted;
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he memorialized to halt the Liaodong campaign;

sentences.zh: 又言京師宗廟所在，願以關中為意。

translations.literal: he also said that the capital was where the ancestral temples stood and expressed the wish that attention be fixed on Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: and urged that since the capital held the ancestral temples, the court should keep its focus on Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 就稿，歎曰：「吾聞男子不死婦人手！

translations.literal: As he finished the draft he sighed and said: "I have heard that a man does not die by a woman's hand!"
translations.idiomatic: Finishing the draft, he sighed, "They say a man should not die by a woman's hand!"

sentences.zh: 」命屏左右，言終卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: " He ordered those at his side to withdraw; having spoken, he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent attendants away, spoke his last words, and died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 將斂，家無珠玉為含，惟貯米五斛、布三十端。

translations.literal: When they were about to enshroud him, the household had no pearls or jade for mouth-placing; there was only stored five hu of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At his laying out the family had no pearls or jade for his mouth—only five hu of rice and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝哭為慟。

translations.literal: The emperor wept in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept in deep grief.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書、秦州都督，諡曰懿，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of War and regional commander of Qinzhou, given the posthumous title Yi, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of War and regional commander of Qinzhou, given the posthumous name Yi, and buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 大亮性忠謹，外若不能言，而內剛烈，不可干非其義。

translations.literal: Daliang's nature was loyal and careful; outwardly he seemed unable to speak, yet inwardly he was fierce and unyielding, and no one could move him from what was not right.
translations.idiomatic: Daliang was loyal and cautious; outwardly he seemed inarticulate, but inwardly he was fierce and would not be swayed from what was right.

sentences.zh: 對天子爭是非，無回撓。

translations.literal: Facing the Son of Heaven he disputed right and wrong without bending or yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Before the emperor he argued right and wrong without yielding.

sentences.zh: 至妻子未始見惰容，事兄嫂以禮聞。

translations.literal: Even toward wife and children he never showed a lazy countenance; his service to elder brother and sister-in-law by ritual was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Even his wife and children never saw him slack; his courtesy toward his elder brother and sister-in-law was famed.

sentences.zh: 位通顯，居陋狹甚。

translations.literal: Though his rank reached eminence, his dwelling was very mean and narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to high rank, his home remained very humble.

sentences.zh: 在越州寫書數百卷，及去，留都督署。

translations.literal: While in Yuezhou he copied several hundred scrolls of books, and when he departed he left them at the commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuezhou he copied several hundred scrolls of books and left them at the commandery when he departed.

sentences.zh: 初，破公祏，以功賜奴婢百口，謂曰：「而曹皆衣冠子女，不幸破亡，吾何忍錄而為隸乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gongshi was defeated, for his merit he was granted a hundred male and female servants; he said to them: "You are all sons and daughters of gentry and officials, unfortunate in ruin—how could I bear to register you as slaves?"
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Gongshi he was rewarded with a hundred servants; he told them, "You are all children of good families ruined by misfortune—how could I make you slaves?"

sentences.zh: 」縱遣之。

translations.literal: " He released and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: " He set them free.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞，咨美，更賜俚婢二十。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard, praised him, and bestowed twenty rustic maidservants in addition.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard and praised him, then gave him twenty rustic maidservants.

sentences.zh: 後破吐谷渾，復賜奴婢百五十口，悉以遺親戚。

translations.literal: Later, when Tuyuhun was defeated, he was again granted a hundred fifty male and female servants, all of whom he gave away to relatives.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Tuyuhun he received another hundred fifty servants and gave them all to relatives.

sentences.zh: 葬宗族無後者三十餘柩，貲襚加焉。

translations.literal: He buried more than thirty coffins of clansmen who had no descendants, supplying funeral goods and shrouds in addition.
translations.idiomatic: He buried more than thirty kinsmen who left no heirs and provided their funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 嘗以張弼脫其死，及貴，念有以報之。

translations.literal: Once Zhang Bi had saved him from death; when he became eminent he thought of repaying him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi had once saved his life; when he rose high he sought to repay him.

sentences.zh: 時弼為將作丞，匿不見，大亮求之不能得。

translations.literal: At that time Bi was assistant director of palace construction and hid himself without appearing; Daliang sought him but could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then assistant director of palace construction and hid from him; Daliang searched but could not find him.

sentences.zh: 一日，識諸塗，持弼泣，悉推家財與之，弼拒不受。

translations.literal: One day he recognized him on the road, seized Bi and wept, and would have pushed all his household wealth upon him, but Bi refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: One day he recognized him on the road, embraced him weeping, and offered all his wealth; Bi refused.

sentences.zh: 乃言於帝曰：「臣及事陛下，張弼力也，願悉臣官爵授之。

translations.literal: He then spoke to the emperor, saying: "Your servant's reaching service to Your Majesty was Zhang Bi's doing; I wish to transfer all my offices and ranks to him."
translations.idiomatic: He told the emperor, "I owe my service to Your Majesty to Zhang Bi; I ask to give him all my offices and titles."

sentences.zh: 」帝為遷弼中郎將、代州都督。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon transferred Bi to gentleman-cadet and regional commander of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor promoted Bi to gentleman-cadet and regional commander of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 世皆賢大亮能報，而多弼不自伐也。

translations.literal: The age all praised Daliang for being able to repay a debt, and many admired Bi for not boasting of himself.
translations.idiomatic: People praised Daliang for repaying a debt and admired Bi for not boasting.

sentences.zh: 歿後，所育孤姓為大亮行服如所親者十餘人。

translations.literal: After his death, more than ten orphans of other surnames whom he had raised wore mourning for him as for a close kin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, more than ten orphans of other surnames he had raised mourned him as kin.

sentences.zh: 兄子 道裕

translations.literal: Nephew Daoyu
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Daoyu

sentences.zh: 兄子道裕，貞觀末為將作匠。

translations.literal: The nephew Daoyu, at the end of Zhenguan, served as director of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu, a nephew, served late in Zhenguan as director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 有告張亮反者，詔百官議。

translations.literal: When someone reported that Zhang Liang was rebelling, an edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Liang was accused of rebellion, the emperor ordered the officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 皆言亮當誅，獨道裕謂反形未具。

translations.literal: All said Liang should be executed; only Daoyu said the signs of rebellion were not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: All said Liang should die; only Daoyu said the evidence of rebellion was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不暇省，斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and had no leisure to examine the matter; he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious, would not listen and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，刑部侍郎缺，宰相屢進名，不可。

translations.literal: After more than a year the vice minister of justice post was vacant; the chief ministers repeatedly put forward names, but none would do.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the vice minister of justice post fell vacant; the chief ministers nominated several candidates, but none satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕得之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have found the man."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have found the man."

sentences.zh: 是嘗議張亮者，朕時雖不從，今尚悔之。

translations.literal: It is the one who once argued over Zhang Liang; though I did not follow him then, I still regret it now.
translations.idiomatic: It is the man who argued over Zhang Liang; I did not heed him then, and I still regret it.

sentences.zh: 」遂命道裕。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed Daoyu.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed Daoyu.

sentences.zh: 終大理卿。

translations.literal: He ended his career as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as chief minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 族孫 迥秀

translations.literal: Clansman grandson Jiongxiu
translations.idiomatic: Clansman grandson Jiongxiu

sentences.zh: 大亮族孫迥秀。

translations.literal: Daliang's clansman grandson Jiongxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu, a clansman grandson of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 迥秀，字茂之。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu, styled Maozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu, courtesy name Maozhi.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，又中英才傑出科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Outstanding Talent category.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and also the Outstanding Talent special examination.

sentences.zh: 調相州參軍事。

translations.literal: He was assigned as aide in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as aide in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累轉考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred and became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit office.

sentences.zh: 武后愛其材，遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: Empress Wu favored his talent and moved him to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu admired his talent and made him attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大足初，檢校夏官侍郎，仍領選，銓汰文武，號稱職，進同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazu he served as acting vice minister of the summer office while still heading selection; in examining civil and military candidates he was said to fulfill his duty, and was advanced to Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace with the Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazu he acted as vice minister of personnel while heading selection; his appointments of civil and military officials were praised as competent, and he was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 張易之兄弟貴驕，因橈意諧媚，士論頓減。

translations.literal: The brothers Zhang Yizhi were noble and arrogant; he bent his will to harmonize and flatter them, and public opinion of him fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang Yizhi brothers were powerful and arrogant; he bent to flatter them, and his reputation among scholars collapsed.

sentences.zh: 俄坐贓貶廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, on a charge of corruption, he was demoted to prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to prefect of Luzhou on a corruption charge.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，貶衡州長史。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, he was demoted to chief administrator of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi was executed, he was demoted to chief administrator of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，召授將作少監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed junior director of palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong ascended the throne, he was recalled as junior director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 累遷鴻臚卿、脩文館學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and academician of the Xiuxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief minister of rites and academician of the Xiuxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 出朔方道行軍大總管，還拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He went out as great campaign commander of the Shuofang Circuit and on return was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as great campaign commander on the Shuofang route and on return was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty, and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 迥秀少聰悟，多通賓客。

translations.literal: Jiongxiu from youth was clever and perceptive and entertained many guests.
translations.idiomatic: Jiongxiu was clever from youth and kept a wide circle of guests.

sentences.zh: 喜飲酒，雖多不亂，當時稱其風流。

translations.literal: He delighted in drinking wine; though he drank much he was never disorderly, and his age called him refined.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine but never lost control however much he drank, and contemporaries praised his easy grace.

sentences.zh: 母少賤，妻嘗詈媵婢，母聞不樂，迥秀即出其妻。

translations.literal: His mother had been of humble birth in youth; his wife once reviled a concubine-servant, and when his mother heard she was displeased; Jiongxiu at once sent his wife away.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been of humble birth; when his wife abused a maid and his mother was upset, Jiongxiu immediately divorced her.

sentences.zh: 或問之，答曰：「娶婦要欲事姑，苟違顏色，何可留？

translations.literal: When someone asked him, he answered: "One takes a wife in order to serve her mother-in-law; if she goes against her countenance, how can she be kept?"
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "A wife is taken to serve her mother-in-law; if she displeases her, how can she stay?"

sentences.zh: 」武后嘗遣內人候其母，或迎置宮中。

translations.literal: " Empress Wu once sent palace women to attend his mother, or had her welcomed and lodged in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu once sent palace women to attend his mother and sometimes had her brought to the palace.

sentences.zh: 後所居堂產芝草，犬乳鄰貓，中宗以為孝感，旌大門閭。

translations.literal: Later in the hall where he lived there grew spirit fungus; a dog nursed a neighbor's cat; Emperor Zhongzong took this as filial feeling moving Heaven and honored his great gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Later spirit fungus grew in his hall, and his dog nursed a neighbor's cat; Zhongzong took this as filial piety moving heaven and honored his household gate.

sentences.zh: 子齊損，開元中以謀逆誅。

translations.literal: His son Qisun, in the Kaiyuan era, was executed on a charge of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qisun was executed in the Kaiyuan era on a charge of treason.

sentences.zh: 戴胄，字玄胤，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Dai Zhou, styled Xuanyin, was a man of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhou, courtesy name Xuanyin, came from Anyang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 性堅正，幹局明強，善簿最。

translations.literal: His nature was firm and upright; in practical affairs he was clear and strong, and skilled at registers and accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and resolute, clear and capable in administration, and expert at accounts.

sentences.zh: 隋末，為門下錄事，納言蘇威、黃門侍郎裴矩厚禮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he served as recorder in the Secretariat; the Counselor Su Wei and the Yellow Gate Vice Director Pei Ju treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Sui he was a recorder in the Secretariat; Su Wei and Pei Ju treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 為越王侗給事郎。

translations.literal: He served as attendant gentleman to Prince Tong of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant gentleman to Prince Tong of Yue.

sentences.zh: 王世充謀篡，胄說曰：「君臣大分均父子，休戚同之。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong plotted usurpation, Zhou admonished him, saying: "The great distinction between ruler and minister equals that between father and son; joy and sorrow are shared alike."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong plotted to seize the throne, Dai Zhou urged him: "The bond between ruler and minister is as weighty as that between father and son; they share the same weal and woe."

sentences.zh: 公當社稷之任，與存與亡，正在今日。

translations.literal: You bear the charge of the altars of soil and grain; whether they survive or perish is decided today.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the fate of the state in your hands; whether the dynasty lives or dies may be decided today.

sentences.zh: 願尊輔王室，擬伊、周以幸天下。

translations.literal: I pray you honor and assist the royal house, model yourself on Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, and bring fortune to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Honor the imperial house, serve as its pillar, and take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as your models, so that the realm may prosper.

sentences.zh: 」世充詭曰：「善。

translations.literal: Shichong dissemblingly said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong answered with feigned agreement: "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」俄肋九錫，胄又切諫，不納。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the Nine Bestowments; Zhou again remonstrated urgently, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shichong accepted the Nine Bestowments; Zhou remonstrated again in the strongest terms, but Shichong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 出為鄭州長史，使與王行本守武牢。

translations.literal: He was sent out as chief administrator of Zheng Prefecture and ordered to hold Hulao together with Wang Xingben.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was posted out as chief administrator of Zheng Prefecture and assigned, with Wang Xingben, to defend Hulao.

sentences.zh: 秦王攻拔之，引為府士曹參軍，封武昌縣男。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin captured it, took him into his staff as a military bureau officer, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin took Hulao, he brought Zhou into his staff as a military bureau officer and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿缺，太宗曰：「大理，人命所系，胄清直，其人哉。

translations.literal: The vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review was vacant. Taizong said: "The Court of Judicial Review—human lives depend on it. Zhou is upright and pure—he is the man."
translations.idiomatic: When the vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review fell vacant, Taizong said: "That court holds men's lives in its hands. Zhou is upright and incorruptible—he is the man for the post."

sentences.zh: 」即日命胄。

translations.literal: That same day Zhou was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Zhou received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌被召，不解佩刀入東上閤。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji was summoned and entered the eastern upper gate office without removing the sword at his belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangsun Wuji was summoned, he entered the eastern upper gate office without taking off the sword at his belt.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射封德彝論監門校尉不覺，罪當死，無忌贖。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Right Feng Deyi held that the gate guard commandant had failed to notice and deserved death, while Wuji could redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Feng Deyi argued that the gate guard commandant, having failed to notice the breach, deserved death, but that Wuji could redeem his offense.

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「校尉與無忌罪均，臣子于尊極不稱誤。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "The commandant and Wuji share equal guilt. Before the sovereign, a subject cannot plead that it was a mistake."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said: "The commandant and Wuji are equally guilty. In the presence of the sovereign, a subject may not excuse himself by calling it an oversight."

sentences.zh: 法著：禦湯劑、飲食、舟船，雖誤皆死。

translations.literal: The law states: for imperial medicines, food, or boats—even if by mistake, death is prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: The law is explicit: for imperial medicines, food, or boats, even an inadvertent offense carries the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 陛下錄無忌功，原之可也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty may record Wuji's merits and pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may weigh Wuji's past service and pardon him.

sentences.zh: 若罰無忌，殺校尉，不可謂刑。

translations.literal: But if you punish Wuji and execute the commandant, this cannot be called justice.
translations.idiomatic: But if Wuji is punished while the commandant alone is executed, that cannot be called impartial justice.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「法為天下公，朕安得阿親戚！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The law is the public affair of the realm—how can I favor my kin!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The law belongs to all under heaven. How could I show partiality to my own kin?"

sentences.zh: 」詔復議，德彝固執，帝將可。

translations.literal: An edict ordered reconsideration. Deyi held firm, and the Emperor was about to assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the case reheard. Deyi stood his ground, and the Emperor was on the point of agreeing.

sentences.zh: 胄曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said: "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 校尉緣無忌以致罪，法當輕；

translations.literal: The commandant incurred guilt because of Wuji—the law should treat him more lightly;
translations.idiomatic: The commandant was drawn into guilt only because of Wuji, and the law should treat him more leniently;

sentences.zh: 若皆誤，不得獨死。

translations.literal: if both were mistaken, the commandant alone must not die.
translations.idiomatic: if both men erred, the commandant alone must not be put to death.

sentences.zh: 」繇是與校尉皆免。

translations.literal: Thereupon both Wuji and the commandant were excused.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis both Wuji and the commandant were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 時選者盛集，有詭資廕冒牒取調者，詔許自首；

translations.literal: When candidates for office were assembled in great numbers, some falsely claimed hereditary privilege or forged credentials to obtain appointment. An edict permitted voluntary confession;
translations.idiomatic: At a time when office seekers were gathered in great numbers, some falsely claimed inherited privilege or forged documents to obtain posts. An edict allowed offenders to confess voluntarily;

sentences.zh: 不首，罪當死。

translations.literal: those who did not confess were to be sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: those who did not confess were to be punished with death.

sentences.zh: 俄有詐得者，獄具，胄以法當流。

translations.literal: Soon there was one caught by fraud; when the case was complete, Zhou held that by law he should be banished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a man who had obtained office by fraud was convicted, and Zhou ruled that under the law he should be banished.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕詔不首者死，而今當流，是示天下不以信，卿賣獄邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "My edict said those who did not confess would die, yet now you sentence him to banishment—this shows the realm that I am not trustworthy. Are you selling judgments?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "My edict declared that those who failed to confess would die, yet now you sentence this man to banishment. That tells the realm I cannot be trusted. Are you corrupting justice?"

sentences.zh: 」胄曰：「陛下登殺之，非臣所及。

translations.literal: Zhou said: "If Your Majesty had personally ordered execution, that would be beyond my reach."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou replied: "If Your Majesty had personally ordered the man's execution, that would lie beyond my authority."

sentences.zh: 既屬臣，敢虧法乎？

translations.literal: Now that the case belongs to me, how dare I violate the law?
translations.idiomatic: But now that the case rests with me, how dare I bend the law?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿自守法，而使我失信，奈何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You keep the law yourself, yet make me break my word—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "You uphold the law, yet you make me break my word. What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 」胄曰：「法者，布大信於人；

translations.literal: Zhou said: "The law spreads great trust among the people;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou said: "The law is what spreads great trust among the people;

sentences.zh: 言乃一時喜怒所發。

translations.literal: words are uttered in a moment's anger or pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: a spoken command is only the product of a moment's anger or pleasure.

sentences.zh: 陛下以一朝忿，將殺之，既知不可而寘於法，此忍小忿、存大信也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, moved by a moment's anger, would have him killed; now knowing it cannot be, you place him within the law—this is swallowing small anger and preserving great trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, in a moment of anger, would have had him killed; now, seeing that this cannot stand, you submit the matter to the law. That is to set aside a small resentment and preserve a great trust.

sentences.zh: 若阿忿違信，臣為陛下惜之。

translations.literal: If you indulge anger and violate trust, I grieve for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty indulges anger at the cost of trust, I fear for what that will cost you.

sentences.zh: 」帝大感寤，從其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply moved and accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply moved and took his advice.

sentences.zh: 胄犯顏據正，數查，參處法意，至析秋毫，隨類指擿，言若泉湧，帝益重之。

translations.literal: Zhou dared to offend his face and uphold what was right; repeatedly investigating cases, he assessed them in the spirit of the law down to splitting an autumn hair; pointing out errors by category, his words flowed like a spring—the Emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou spoke bluntly to the Emperor's face and held to what was right. He examined case after case, judging each in the true spirit of the law down to the finest detail, exposing faults wherever they fell. His words poured forth like a spring, and the Emperor came to rely on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 矜其貧，特詔賜錢十萬。

translations.literal: Taking pity on his poverty, the Emperor specially decreed a gift of one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his poverty, the Emperor issued a special edict granting him one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 會僕射蕭瑀免，封德彝卒，帝謂胄曰：「尚書總國綱維，失一事，天下有受其弊者。

translations.literal: When Director Xiao Yu was dismissed and Feng Deyi died, the Emperor said to Zhou: "The Imperial Secretariat holds the great cables of state; one oversight and people throughout the realm suffer from it."
translations.idiomatic: When Director Xiao Yu was dismissed and Feng Deyi died, the Emperor told Zhou: "The Imperial Secretariat holds the cables of the state. One misstep there, and people across the realm feel the harm."

sentences.zh: 今以令、僕委卿，宜副朕舉。

translations.literal: Now I entrust the posts of Director and Vice Director to you—you must live up to my selection.
translations.idiomatic: I now entrust the directorship and vice directorship to you. You must prove worthy of my choice.

sentences.zh: 」胄明敏，長於操決，無宿疑。

translations.literal: Zhou was bright and quick, skilled at making decisions, with no lingering doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was sharp and quick-minded, decisive in action, and never left matters unresolved.

sentences.zh: 議者美其振職，謂武德以來殆無其輩。

translations.literal: Commentators praised his revitalization of the office, saying that since the Wude era there had scarcely been his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Observers praised the vigor with which he revived the office, saying that since the Wude era there had scarcely been anyone to match him.

sentences.zh: 復拜諫議大夫，與魏徵更日供奉。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Remonstrance Adviser and, with Wei Zheng, attended the emperor on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Remonstrance Adviser and, with Wei Zheng, attended the emperor on alternate days.

sentences.zh: 進民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 杜如晦遺言，請以選舉委胄，由是檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui's dying words asked that appointments be entrusted to Zhou; for this reason he was made acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In his dying words Du Ruhui asked that appointments be entrusted to Zhou, and on that basis Zhou was made acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 然好抑文雅，獎法吏，時以寡學為訾。

translations.literal: Yet he liked to suppress literary men and reward legal officials; at the time he was criticized for limited learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he tended to hold back men of letters and favor legal officials, and at the time he was criticized for lack of broad learning.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，以本官參豫朝政，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan, with his existing office he joined in deliberating court policy and was advanced to the rank of Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he took part in court deliberations in his existing capacity and was raised to Duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝將脩復洛陽宮，胄上疏諫曰：「比關中、河外置軍圍，強夫富室悉為兵，九成之役又興，司農、將作見丁無幾。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to repair the Luoyang palace. Zhou submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Lately military encampments have been set up in Guanzhong and beyond the Yellow River; strong men and wealthy households have all become soldiers; work on Jiucheng has also begun—the Ministries of Revenue and Public Works have scarcely any laborers available."
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor planned to restore the Luoyang palace, Zhou submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Recently military camps have been established in Guanzhong and beyond the Yellow River. Able men and wealthy households have all been turned into soldiers, and work on Jiucheng has begun again. The Ministries of Revenue and Public Works scarcely have laborers left."

sentences.zh: 大亂之後，戶口單破，一人就役，舉室捐業。

translations.literal: After the great chaos, households are thin and broken; when one man takes up labor service, the whole family abandons its livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: After the great upheaval households are depleted and broken. When one man is called to labor, the whole family loses its livelihood.

sentences.zh: 籍軍者督戎仗，課役者責糧齎，竭貲經紀，猶不能濟。

translations.literal: Those registered for the army are pressed for weapons; those levied for labor are charged with grain—exhausting their wealth in managing affairs, they still cannot manage.
translations.idiomatic: Those enrolled in the army are pressed for weapons; those levied for labor are charged with grain. They exhaust their resources just to get by, yet still cannot meet their obligations.

sentences.zh: 七月以來，霖潦未止，濱河南北，田正洿下，年之有亡未可知。

translations.literal: Since the seventh month rains and floods have not ceased; along both banks of the Yellow River the fields lie waterlogged—whether there will be a harvest is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Since the seventh month rains and floods have not stopped. Along both banks of the Yellow River the fields stand waterlogged, and no one can tell whether there will be a harvest this year.

sentences.zh: 壯者盡行，賦調不給，則帑藏虛矣。

translations.literal: If all able-bodied men depart and taxes and levies go unmet, the treasury will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: If every able-bodied man is sent away and taxes and levies cannot be collected, the treasury will be emptied.

sentences.zh: 今宮殿足庇風雨、容羽衛，數年後成，猶不謂晚，何憚而遽自生勞擾邪？

translations.literal: The present palace suffices to shelter from wind and rain and house the imperial guard; completion in several years would still not be late—why shrink from waiting and hastily create labor and disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: The present palace is enough to keep out wind and rain and to house the imperial guard. If it were finished only after several years, that would still not be late. Why shrink from delay and hastily bring labor and hardship on the people?

sentences.zh: 」帝覽奏，罷役。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and canceled the project.

sentences.zh: 胄所敷內，緣政得失，咸有可觀。

translations.literal: In what Zhou presented within the court, his accounts of governmental gains and losses were all worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: In the counsel Zhou offered within the court, his accounts of what government had done well or ill were always worth reading.

sentences.zh: 奏已，即削稿，秘外莫知。

translations.literal: Once submitted, he at once destroyed the draft; those outside knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Once a memorial was submitted, he destroyed the draft at once, so those outside the court never knew its contents.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂左右曰：「胄於我非肺腑親，然事之機切無不聞，惟其忠概所激耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once told those around him: "Zhou is no close kin of mine, yet on all urgent matters of state he has spoken without reserve—solely stirred by his loyal forthrightness."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once told those around him: "Zhou is no kinsman of mine, yet on every urgent matter he speaks without holding back. That comes only from the force of his loyal integrity."

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，帝為舉哀，贈尚書右僕射，追封道國公，諡曰忠；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died. The Emperor mourned him, posthumously appointing him Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, enfeoffing him posthumously as Duke of Daoguo, with the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died. The Emperor mourned him, posthumously appointing him Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, raising him to Duke of Daoguo, and giving him the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 以第舍陋不容祭，詔有司為立廟。

translations.literal: Because his residence was too mean for sacrifices, the Emperor ordered the relevant offices to erect a temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his house was too small to serve for sacrifices, the Emperor ordered the proper offices to build him a temple.

sentences.zh: 聘其女為道王妃。

translations.literal: His daughter was recruited as consort to the Prince of Dao.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was taken in marriage as consort to the Prince of Dao.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡、魏徵與胄善，每至生平故處，輒流涕。
