translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng were on good terms with Zhou; whenever they came to places from his life, they would weep.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Wei Zheng were close to Zhou, and whenever they passed places associated with his life they would weep.

sentences.zh: 胄無子，以兄子至德為後。

translations.literal: Zhou had no son; he took his elder brother's son Zhide as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had no son and adopted his elder brother's son Zhide as his heir.

sentences.zh: 侄 至德

translations.literal: Nephew: Zhide
translations.idiomatic: Nephew: Zhide

sentences.zh: 至德，乾封中累遷西台侍郎、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: Zhide, during the Qianfeng era, was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Western Terrace and participant in the third rank of both eastern and western terraces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfeng era Zhide rose through repeated promotions to Vice Director of the Western Terrace and third-rank participant on both the Eastern and Western Terraces.

sentences.zh: 閱十數年，父子繼為宰相，世詫其榮。

translations.literal: Within a dozen years, father and son successively served as chancellors; the age marveled at their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than a decade, father and son served as chancellor in succession, and the age marveled at their honor.

sentences.zh: 高宗嘗為飛白書賜侍臣，賜至德曰：「泛洪源，俟舟楫」，郝處俊曰：「飛九霄，假六翮」，李敬玄曰「資啟沃，罄丹誠」，崔知悌曰「竭忠節，贊皇猷」，皆見意於辭云。

translations.literal: Gaozong once wrote in flying-white script to grant to attending ministers; to Zhide he wrote: "Spread upon the great source, await oars and rudders." Hao Chujun said: "Soar nine heavens, borrow six pinions." Li Jingxuan said: "Supply counsel and nurture, exhaust crimson loyalty." Cui Zhitì said: "Exhaust loyal integrity, aid the imperial plan." Each expressed his meaning in the wording.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong once wrote in flying-white script for his attending ministers. To Zhide he wrote: "Spread upon the great source, await oars and rudders." Hao Chujun wrote: "Soar nine heavens, borrow six pinions." Li Jingxuan wrote: "Supply counsel and nurture, exhaust crimson loyalty." Cui Zhitì wrote: "Exhaust loyal integrity, aid the imperial plan." Each man's words revealed his intent.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時劉仁軌為左，人有所訴，率優容之；

translations.literal: At the time Liu Rengui held the left post; when people brought complaints, he generally treated them leniently;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Rengui held the left vice directorship. When people brought complaints, he generally treated them with indulgence;

sentences.zh: 至德乃詰究本末，理直者密為奏，終不顯私恩。

translations.literal: Zhide would then investigate the rights and wrongs from start to finish; when someone was in the right he secretly submitted a memorial, never openly showing private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide would then investigate the matter from beginning to end. When someone was in the right, he submitted a private memorial on his behalf, but never openly showed personal favor.

sentences.zh: 由是，當時多稱仁軌者，號仁軌為「解事僕射」。

translations.literal: Hence many at the time praised Rengui, calling him the "Vice Director Who Gets Things Done."
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many at the time praised Rengui and called him the "Vice Director Who Gets Things Done."

sentences.zh: 嘗更日聽訟，有嫗詣省，至德已收牒，嫗乃復取，曰：「初以為解事僕射，今乃非是。

translations.literal: Once on their day to hear lawsuits, an old woman came to the Secretariat; Zhide had already taken her petition, but the woman took it back, saying: "At first I thought you were the Vice Director Who Gets Things Done—now I see you are not."
translations.idiomatic: Once, on the day they alternated in hearing lawsuits, an old woman came to the Secretariat. Zhide had already taken her petition, but she took it back and said: "At first I thought you were the Vice Director Who Gets Things Done. Now I see you are not."

sentences.zh: 」至德笑還之。

translations.literal: Zhide smiled and returned it to her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide smiled and gave it back to her.

sentences.zh: 人伏其長者。

translations.literal: People admired his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 或以問，至德答曰：「慶賞刑罰，人主之柄，為臣豈得與人主爭也！

translations.literal: When someone asked him about it, Zhide replied: "Rewards and punishments are the sovereign's handle—how can a minister contend with the sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked him about it, Zhide replied: "Rewards and punishments are the sovereign's prerogative. How can a minister contend with the sovereign over them?"

sentences.zh: 」帝知，歎美之。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned of it and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of this, he sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年卒，詔百官哭其第。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng he died; an edict ordered the hundred officials to mourn at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Yifeng, and an edict ordered the officials to mourn at his house.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master with Splendid Opening Honours and Military Commissioner of Bingzhou; his posthumous name was Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master with Splendid Opening Honours and Military Commissioner of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 劉洎，字思道，荊州江陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, styled Sidao, was a native of Jiangling in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, styled Sidao, was a native of Jiangling in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為蕭銑黃門侍郎，南略地嶺表，下五十城，未還而銑敗，遂以城自歸，授南康州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Initially he served Xiao Xian as Vice Director in the Yellow Gate; he marched south to seize territory in Lingnan and captured fifty cities. Before he returned, Xian was defeated; he thereupon surrendered the cities and was appointed chief administrator of the Nankang Prefecture military commission.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served Xiao Xian as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate. He marched south into Lingnan and took fifty cities. Before he could return, Xian was defeated, so he surrendered the cities and was appointed chief administrator of the Nankang military commission.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，擢給事中，封清苑縣男，轉治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Supervising Censor-in-Attendance, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan County, and transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan he was promoted to Supervising Censor-in-Attendance, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan County, and transferred to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 于時，尚書省詔敕稽壅，按成復下，彌年不能決。

translations.literal: At that time, imperial edicts and orders in the Imperial Secretariat piled up in delay; cases completed and sent down again could not be decided for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: At that time edicts and orders in the Imperial Secretariat piled up in delay. Cases completed and sent down again might remain undecided for a full year.

sentences.zh: 洎言：「尚書，萬機本，貞觀初未有令、僕，職並務繁，左丞戴胄、右丞魏征，應事彈舉，無所回橈，百司震肅不敢懈。

translations.literal: Ji said: "The Imperial Secretariat is the root of the myriad affairs of state. At the beginning of Zhenguan there were no Directors or Vice Directors; duties were all heavy. Left Vice Director Dai Zhou and Right Vice Director Wei Zheng, responding to affairs with impeachment and prosecution, bent to nothing; the hundred offices were awed into discipline and dared not slacken."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "The Imperial Secretariat is the root of the myriad affairs of state. At the beginning of Zhenguan there were no directors or vice directors, and every duty was heavy. Left Vice Director Dai Zhou and Right Vice Director Wei Zheng met each matter with impeachment and prosecution, yielding to no one. The hundred offices were awed into discipline and dared not slacken."

sentences.zh: 比者勳親在位，品非其任，功勢相傾，雖欲自強，先懼囂謗。

translations.literal: Lately meritorious kin have held office; their rank does not match their duties; merit and power press against each other; though they wish to exert themselves, they first fear noisy slander.
translations.idiomatic: Lately meritorious kinsmen have held office whose rank does not match their duties. Merit and power press against one another, and though men wish to exert themselves, they first fear clamorous slander.

sentences.zh: 故郎中嘿奪，惟事咨稟；

translations.literal: Hence bureau directors silently yield their authority and only consult and report upward;
translations.idiomatic: For this reason bureau directors silently surrender their authority and do nothing but consult and report upward;

sentences.zh: 尚書依違，不得專裁。

translations.literal: the directors of the Secretariat waver and cannot decide independently.
translations.idiomatic: while the directors of the Secretariat hesitate and cannot decide on their own.

sentences.zh: 管轄玩弛，綱紀不振。

translations.literal: Jurisdiction grows lax and slack; discipline is not restored.
translations.idiomatic: Jurisdiction grows slack and discipline is no longer enforced.

sentences.zh: 今宜精選左右丞、兩司郎中，使皆得人，非惟救曠滯之弊，固當矯拂趨競也。

translations.literal: Now one should carefully select the left and right vice directors and the bureau directors of both departments, ensuring that all are the right men—not only to remedy the harm of backlog and delay, but also to correct and restrain the rush for rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Now the left and right vice directors and the bureau directors of both departments should be carefully chosen so that each post is filled by the right man. That would not only remedy the backlog, but also check the scramble for advancement.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 洎健于職，於是尚書復治如征時。

translations.literal: Ji was vigorous in his duties; the Secretariat was again well governed as in Zheng's time.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was vigorous in office, and the Secretariat was again well governed as it had been in Wei Zheng's day.

sentences.zh: 累加銀青光祿大夫、散騎常侍，攝黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was progressively granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Regular Attendant, and acted as Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively granted the titles Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture and Regular Attendant, and served as acting Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗好持論，與公卿言古今事，必往復難詰、究臧否。

translations.literal: Taizong loved to hold to argument; when speaking with ministers about affairs ancient and modern, he always went back and forth with hard questioning, examining right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong loved to argue. When he discussed past and present affairs with his ministers, he always pressed them back and forth with hard questions, probing right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 洎諫曰：「帝王之與臣庶，聖哲之與庸愚，等級遼絕，勢不倫擬。

translations.literal: Ji remonstrated: "Between emperor and common subject, between sage and fool—the grades are vastly separated; their positions cannot be likened."
translations.idiomatic: Ji remonstrated: "Between emperor and subject, between sage and fool, the distance in rank is vast and their positions cannot be compared."

sentences.zh: 故課愚對聖，持卑抗尊，雖思自強，不可得已。

translations.literal: Hence to set the foolish in debate against the sage, holding the low to contend with the high—even if one wishes to exert oneself, it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: To set the foolish in debate against the sage, or the humble in contention against the exalted—even if one wishes to hold one's own, it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 陛下降慈旨，假柔顏，虛心聽納，猶恐群臣惴縮不敢進。

translations.literal: Your Majesty lowers kind intent and lends a gentle countenance, listening with an open mind—yet one still fears the ministers will shrink in trepidation and not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Your Majesty lowers a gracious intent, shows a gentle face, and listens with an open mind, one still fears the ministers will shrink back and not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 況以神機天辯，飾辭援古而迮其議哉！

translations.literal: How much more when with divine wit and heaven-sent eloquence you polish your words, cite antiquity, and press their arguments!
translations.idiomatic: How much less when Your Majesty, with divine wit and heaven-sent eloquence, polishes your words, cites antiquity, and presses their arguments!

sentences.zh: 夫天以無言為尊，聖以不言為德，皆弗欲煩也。

translations.literal: Heaven is honored through silence; the sage is virtuous through not speaking—both wish to avoid vexation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is honored through silence; the sage is virtuous through restraint in speech—both seek to avoid needless trouble.

sentences.zh: 且多記損心，多語耗氣，心氣內損，形神外勞，初雖無覺，久且為弊。

translations.literal: Moreover, much remembering harms the heart; much speaking exhausts the breath—heart and breath depleted within, form and spirit wearied without; at first one may not notice, but in time it becomes harm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, much remembering wears on the heart, and much speaking drains the breath. Heart and breath are depleted within, body and spirit are worn without. At first one may not notice, but in time it becomes a real harm.

sentences.zh: 且今之雍平，陛下力行所至耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, today's peace and prosperity are simply what Your Majesty's strenuous effort has achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the peace and prosperity of today are simply the fruit of Your Majesty's own strenuous effort.

sentences.zh: 欲其長久，匪由辯博，但當忘愛憎，慎取捨，若貞觀初可矣！

translations.literal: To make it endure long, it does not lie in eloquence and erudition—one need only forget likes and dislikes, be careful in choosing and rejecting, as at the beginning of Zhenguan—and that will suffice!
translations.idiomatic: If you wish it to endure, that will not come from eloquence and erudition. You need only put aside likes and dislikes, choose and reject with care, as at the beginning of Zhenguan—and that will be enough!

sentences.zh: 」手詔答曰：「非慮無以臨下，非言無以述慮。

translations.literal: A hand edict replied: "Without concern one cannot oversee subordinates; without words one cannot express concern."
translations.idiomatic: A hand edict replied: "Without concern one cannot oversee subordinates; without words one cannot express that concern."

sentences.zh: 雖然，驕人輕物，恐由榷論致之。

translations.literal: Even so, arrogance toward others and slighting things—I fear these may come from pressing debate.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I fear that arrogance toward others and contempt for things may come from pressing debate too far.

sentences.zh: 若形神心氣，不為勞也。」

translations.literal: If form, spirit, heart, and breath are not worn by it, [so be it.]"
translations.idiomatic: If body, spirit, heart, and breath are not worn by it, then so be it."

sentences.zh: 皇太子初立，洎謂宜尊賢重道，上書曰：「太子宗祧是系，善惡之習，興亡在焉。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was first installed, Ji said one should honor the worthy and respect the Way, and submitted a memorial saying: "Upon the Heir Apparent the ancestral shrine depends; habits of good and evil, rise and fall are therein."
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was first installed, Ji argued that the court should honor the worthy and respect the Way, and submitted a memorial saying: "Upon the Heir Apparent the ancestral line depends; habits of good and evil, and the rise or fall of the dynasty, all rest therein."

sentences.zh: 弗勤於始，將悔於末。

translations.literal: If one is not diligent at the beginning, one will regret at the end.
translations.idiomatic: If one is not diligent at the start, one will regret it at the end.

sentences.zh: 故晁錯上書，令通政術；

translations.literal: Hence Chao Cuo submitted a memorial, making him master statecraft;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Chao Cuo submitted a memorial to make the heir master the arts of government;

sentences.zh: 賈誼奏計，務知禮教。

translations.literal: Jia Yi presented plans, urging knowledge of ritual and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: and Jia Yi presented plans, urging that he learn ritual and moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 今太子孝友仁愛，挺自天姿，然春秋鼎盛，學當有漸。

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince is filial, fraternal, benevolent, and loving; upright by inborn nature. Yet in the prime of youth, learning should proceed by stages.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Crown Prince is filial, fraternal, benevolent, and loving by inborn nature. Yet in the prime of youth, his education should proceed step by step.

sentences.zh: 以陛下多才多藝，尚垂精厲志，以博異聞，而太子優遊，坐棄白日。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty, with many talents and many skills, still bends your spirit and sharpens your will to broaden strange knowledge, yet the Crown Prince drifts at ease, sitting and wasting the bright days.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with many talents and skills, still bends your spirit and sharpens your will to broaden your learning, yet the Crown Prince drifts at ease and lets the bright days go to waste.

sentences.zh: 陛下每退朝，引見群臣，訪以今古，咨以得失；

translations.literal: Each time Your Majesty leaves court, you summon ministers, inquire about past and present, consult on gains and losses;
translations.idiomatic: Each time Your Majesty leaves court, you summon your ministers, inquire about past and present affairs, and consult them on what succeeds and what fails;

sentences.zh: 而太子處內，不接正人，不聞正論，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: yet the Crown Prince stays within, meets no upright men, hears no upright discourse—what your servant cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: yet the Crown Prince remains within the palace, meets no upright men, and hears no upright discourse. That is what your servant cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 古者，問安而退，以廣敬也；

translations.literal: In antiquity, one inquired after health and withdrew, to extend reverence;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity one inquired after the sovereign's health and then withdrew, so as to extend reverence;

sentences.zh: 異宮而處，以遠嫌也。

translations.literal: dwelt in a separate palace, to keep suspicion at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: and dwelt in a separate palace, so as to keep suspicion at a distance.

sentences.zh: 間者，太子一入侍，逾句不出，師傅寮采，具員而已，非所謂愛之也。

translations.literal: Recently the Crown Prince once entered attendance and for more than ten days did not come out; teachers, tutors, and staff merely filled their posts—this is not what is called loving him.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Crown Prince entered attendance once and did not come out for more than ten days. His teachers, tutors, and staff merely filled their posts. This is not what is called truly loving him.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為授以良書，娛以佳賓，使耳所未聞，睹所未見，儲德愈光，群生之福也。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks: grant him good books, entertain him with fine guests, let him hear what his ears have never heard and see what his eyes have never seen—stored virtue would grow brighter; it would be the blessing of all living beings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly believes that if he were given good books and entertained with worthy guests, so that he heard what his ears had never heard and saw what his eyes had never seen, his stored virtue would grow brighter—and that would be a blessing for all the people.

sentences.zh: 」帝於是敕洎與岑文本、馬周遞日直東宮。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then ordered Ji, together with Cen Wenben and Ma Zhou, to serve at the Eastern Palace on rotating days.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then ordered Ji, together with Cen Wenben and Ma Zhou, to attend the Eastern Palace on alternating days.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怒苑西監穆裕，有詔斬朝堂，皇太子驟諫。

translations.literal: The Emperor once grew angry at Mu Yu, superintendent of the western park, and issued an edict to execute him in the court hall; the Crown Prince urgently remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once grew angry at Mu Yu, superintendent of the western park, and issued an edict to execute him in the court hall. The Crown Prince urgently remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「朕始得魏征，朝夕進諫。

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure: "When I first obtained Wei Zheng, morning and evening he advanced remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said with pleasure: "When I first obtained Wei Zheng, morning and evening he offered remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 征亡，劉洎、岑文本、馬周、褚遂良繼之。

translations.literal: When Zheng died, Liu Ji, Cen Wenben, Ma Zhou, and Chu Suiliang succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng died, Liu Ji, Cen Wenben, Ma Zhou, and Chu Suiliang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 兒在吾膝前，見朕悅諫熟矣，故有今日言也。

translations.literal: My son before my knees has seen me pleased with remonstrance until he knows it well; hence today's words.
translations.idiomatic: My son at my knee has seen me pleased with remonstrance until he knows it well. That is why he spoke as he did today.

sentences.zh: 誠習以性成哉！

translations.literal: Truly, habit becomes nature!
translations.idiomatic: Truly, habit becomes second nature!

sentences.zh: 」稍遷侍中。

translations.literal: " He was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji was gradually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 帝忽謂群臣曰：「朕今欲聞己過，卿等為朕言之。

translations.literal: The Emperor suddenly said to the ministers: "I now wish to hear my faults; you shall speak them for me.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suddenly said to the ministers: "I now wish to hear my faults. Speak of them for me.

sentences.zh: 」長孫無忌、李勣、楊師道同辭對曰：「陛下以盛德致太平，臣等愚不見其過。

translations.literal: " Zhangsun Wuji, Li Ji, and Yang Shidao together replied: "Your Majesty with flourishing virtue brought about Great Peace; we are foolish and see no fault."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangsun Wuji, Li Ji, and Yang Shidao replied together: "Your Majesty, with flourishing virtue, brought about Great Peace. We are too dull to see any fault."

sentences.zh: 」洎曰：「然頃上書有不稱旨，或面窮詰，無不羞汗，恐非所以進言者路。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Yet recently when memorials did not accord with intent, or one was pressed in person with exhaustive questioning, none failed to flush with shame and sweat—I fear this is not the path by which speakers advance."
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said: "Yet recently, when memorials did not accord with Your Majesty's intent, or when one was pressed in person with exhaustive questioning, no one failed to flush with shame and sweat. I fear this is not the path by which men dare speak up."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「卿言善，朕能改之。」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Your words are good; I can change."
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "Your words are good. I can change."

sentences.zh: 及征遼東，詔兼太子左庶子、檢校民部尚書，輔皇太子監國。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, he was ordered to serve concurrently as Left Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent and acting Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, assisting the Crown Prince in overseeing the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, he was ordered to serve concurrently as Left Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent and acting Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, assisting the Crown Prince in overseeing the state.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以卿輔太子，社稷安危在焉，宜識朕意。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "With you assisting the Crown Prince, the safety or peril of the altars of soil and grain rests therein—you should understand my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "With you assisting the Crown Prince, the safety or peril of the altars of soil and grain rests upon you. You should understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 」洎曰：「願無憂！

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Wish no worry!
translations.idiomatic: " Ji said: "Have no worry!

sentences.zh: 即大臣有罪，臣謹按法誅之。

translations.literal: Even if great ministers are guilty, your servant will carefully punish them according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Even if great ministers are guilty, your servant will strictly punish them according to law."

sentences.zh: 」帝怪其語謬，戒曰：「君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thought his words absurd and warned him: "If the ruler is not discreet he loses his ministers; if the minister is not discreet he loses his person.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thought his words absurd and warned him: "If the ruler is not discreet, he loses his ministers; if the minister is not discreet, he loses his life.

sentences.zh: 卿性疏而果，恐以此敗。

translations.literal: Your nature is loose and rash—I fear you will fail because of this."
translations.idiomatic: Your nature is loose and rash. I fear you will come to ruin because of this."

sentences.zh: 」洎與褚遂良不相中。

translations.literal: " Ji and Chu Suiliang did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji and Chu Suiliang did not get along.

sentences.zh: 帝還，不豫，洎與馬周入候，出見遂良，泣曰：「上體患癰，殊可懼！

translations.literal: The Emperor returned, fell ill; Ji and Ma Zhou entered to attend him. Coming out they met Suiliang and wept: "The sovereign's body suffers from a carbuncle—truly fearful!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned, he fell ill. Ji and Ma Zhou went in to attend him, and on coming out met Suiliang and wept: "The sovereign's body suffers from a carbuncle. It is truly alarming!"

sentences.zh: 」遂良即誣奏「洎曰：國家不足慮，正當輔少主行伊、霍事，大臣有異者，誅之。

translations.literal: " Suiliang immediately slanderously memorialized: "Ji said: The state is not worth worrying about; one should only assist the young lord and act the part of Yi and Huo. Any great minister who disagrees—execute him."
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang immediately submitted a slanderous memorial: "Ji said: The state is not worth worrying about. One should only assist the young lord and act the part of Yi Yin and Huo Guang. Any great minister who disagrees should be executed."

sentences.zh: 」帝愈，召洎問狀，洎引馬周為左。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor recovered, he summoned Ji to question the matter; Ji cited Ma Zhou as witness.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor recovered, he summoned Ji to question him about the charge. Ji cited Ma Zhou as his witness.

sentences.zh: 遂良執不已，帝惑之，乃賜死。

translations.literal: Suiliang persisted without letup; the Emperor was confused by it and ordered death by suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang persisted without letup. The Emperor was swayed by it and ordered Ji to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 方死時，索筆牘，欲自言，有司不敢與。

translations.literal: At the time of death he asked for brush and paper, wishing to speak for himself; the officials dared not provide them.
translations.idiomatic: As he was dying, he asked for brush and paper, wishing to speak in his own defense, but the officials dared not give them to him.

sentences.zh: 帝后知之，有司皆得罪。

translations.literal: When the Emperor later learned of it, the officials were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor later learned of this, all the officials involved were punished.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，其子弘業詣闕訴遂良譖死狀，李義府右之。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era, his son Hongye came to the court to appeal the circumstances of Suiliang's slanderous death; Li Yifu sided with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianqing era, his son Hongye came to the court to appeal the circumstances of Suiliang's slanderous death. Li Yifu sided with him.

sentences.zh: 高宗問近臣，給事中樂彥瑋曰：「辨之，是暴先帝過刑。

translations.literal: Gaozong asked nearby ministers; Supervising Secretary Yue Yanwei said: "To investigate would be to expose the late emperor's excessive punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong asked his nearby ministers. Supervising Secretary Yue Yanwei said: "To investigate would be to expose the late emperor's excessive punishment."

sentences.zh: 」事寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 文明初，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wenming, an edict restored his office and titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wenming era, an edict restored his office and titles.

sentences.zh: 附 樂彥瑋

translations.literal: Appended: [Biography of] Yue Yanwei
translations.idiomatic: Appended: [Biography of] Yue Yanwei

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「劉洎之才之烈，《易》所謂「王臣蹇蹇」者。

translations.literal: The encomium says: "In talent and fiery loyalty Liu Ji was what the Changes calls 'the king's minister, steadfast and firm.'"
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: "In talent and fiery loyalty Liu Ji was what the Book of Changes calls 'the king's minister, steadfast and firm.'"

sentences.zh: 然性剛疏，輔太子，欲身任安危，以言掩其眾，為媢忌所乘，卒陷罪誅。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stiff and loose; assisting the Crown Prince, he wished to personally bear safety and peril, using words to cover the multitude—seized upon by jealous enmity, he finally fell into crime and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was stiff and undisciplined. While assisting the Crown Prince, he wished to bear the state's safety and peril himself and used bold words to overshadow others. Seized upon by jealous enemies, he finally fell into crime and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 以太宗之明，蔽於所忿，洎之忠不能自申於上，況其下哉？

translations.literal: Even with Taizong's brilliance, blinded by what enraged him, Ji's loyalty could not declare itself to the sovereign—how much less for those below!
translations.idiomatic: Even with Taizong's brilliance, blinded by what enraged him, Ji's loyalty could not make itself heard above—how much less can it be heard below!

sentences.zh: 古人以言為戒，可不慎歟！

translations.literal: The ancients took words as a warning—can one not be careful!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients took words as a warning. Can one not be careful!

sentences.zh: 崔仁師

translations.literal: Cui Renshi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Renshi

sentences.zh: 崔仁師，定州安喜人。

translations.literal: Cui Renshi was a man of Anxi in Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Renshi was a native of Anxi in Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武德初擢制舉，調管州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was raised through the decree examination and was appointed Recording Officer of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude era he passed the decree examination and was appointed recording officer of Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳叔達薦仁師才任史官，遷右武衛錄事參軍，與脩梁、魏史。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda recommended Renshi's talent for service as historiographer; he was transferred to Recording Officer of the Right Martial Guard and joined in compiling the histories of Liang and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda recommended Renshi as talented enough to serve as a historiographer. He was transferred to recording officer of the Right Martial Guard and helped compile the histories of Liang and Wei.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，改殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was changed to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenguan era he was made a palace censor.

sentences.zh: 時青州有男子謀逆，有司捕支黨，累系填獄，詔仁師按覆。

translations.literal: At the time in Qing Prefecture a man plotted rebellion; the officials arrested his associates; prisoners piled up filling the prisons; an edict ordered Renshi to review the case.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a man in Qing Prefecture plotted rebellion. The officials arrested his associates until the prisons were packed full. An edict ordered Renshi to review the case.

sentences.zh: 始至，悉去囚械，為具食，飲湯瀋，以情訊之，坐止魁惡十餘人，它悉原縱。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, he removed all prisoners' shackles, provided food for them, gave hot water for bathing, and questioned them according to the facts; only about a dozen ringleaders and evildoers were convicted; all others were pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived, he removed all the prisoners' shackles, provided them with food and hot water for bathing, and questioned them according to the facts. Only about a dozen ringleaders and evildoers were convicted; all the rest were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿孫伏伽謂曰：「原雪者眾，誰肯讓死？

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Sun Fugai said to him: "Those pardoned and cleared are many—who would willingly accept death?
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Sun Fugai said to him: "You have pardoned and cleared so many. Who would willingly accept death?

sentences.zh: 就決而事變，奈何？

translations.literal: If you decide now and affairs change, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: If you decide the case now and affairs later change, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」仁師曰：「治獄主仁恕，故諺稱'殺人刖足，亦皆有禮'。

translations.literal: " Renshi said: "Governing prisons rests on benevolence and forbearance; hence the proverb says, 'Even in killing a man or cutting off a foot, there is always propriety.'
translations.idiomatic: " Renshi said: "Governing prisons rests on benevolence and forbearance. Hence the proverb says, 'Even in killing a man or cutting off a foot, there is always propriety.'

sentences.zh: 豈有知枉不申，為身謀哉？

translations.literal: How could one, knowing the wrongly condemned are not cleared, scheme for one's own person?
translations.idiomatic: How could one, knowing the innocent are not cleared, scheme only for one's own safety?

sentences.zh: 使吾以一介易十囚命，固吾願也！

translations.literal: If I could exchange one poor body for ten prisoners' lives, that would indeed be my wish!"
translations.idiomatic: If I could exchange my one poor body for the lives of ten prisoners, that would indeed be my wish!"

sentences.zh: 」及敕使覆訊，諸囚咸叩頭曰：「崔公仁恕，必無枉者。

translations.literal: " When imperial emissaries came to re-examine, all prisoners kowtowed and said: "Lord Cui is benevolent and forbearing; there will surely be no wrongful cases."
translations.idiomatic: " When imperial emissaries came to re-examine the case, all the prisoners kowtowed and said: "Lord Cui is benevolent and forbearing. There will surely be no wrongful convictions."

sentences.zh: 」舉無異辭。

translations.literal: " All testified without discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: " All testified without discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became renowned.

sentences.zh: 遷度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to bureau director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 嘗口陳移用費數千名，太宗怪之，詔黃門侍郎杜正倫持簿，使仁師對唱，無一謬。

translations.literal: Once he orally recited several thousand items of transferred expenditures; Taizong was astonished and ordered Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Du Zhenglun to hold the ledger and have Renshi match and recite them aloud—not one error.
translations.idiomatic: Once he orally recited several thousand items of transferred expenditures from memory. Taizong was astonished and ordered Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Du Zhenglun to hold the ledger while Renshi matched and recited each item aloud. Not one was wrong.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 時校書郎王玄度注《尚書》、《毛詩》，抵孔、鄭舊學，請遂廢。

translations.literal: At the time Proofreader Wang Xuandu annotated the Documents and Mao's Odes, opposing the old learning of Kong and Zheng, and requested they be abolished forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Proofreader Wang Xuandu annotated the Documents and Mao's Odes, attacking the old learning of Kong Yingda and Zheng Xuan, and requested that their commentaries be abolished.

sentences.zh: 詔諸儒大議，博士以下不能詰。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Confucian scholars to great debate; those below the rank of erudite could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned the Confucian scholars to debate the matter at length. Even those below the rank of erudite could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 河間王孝恭請與孔、鄭並行，仁師以玄度不經，條不合大義者奏之。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Hejian requested that Kong and Zheng proceed in parallel; Renshi, holding that Xuandu's work was unsound, memorialized article by article where it did not accord with great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Hejian requested that Kong and Zheng be allowed to proceed in parallel. Renshi, holding that Xuandu's work was unsound, memorialized point by point where it failed to accord with great principle.

sentences.zh: 玄度報罷。

translations.literal: Xuandu's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandu's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時有司以律「反逆者緣坐兄弟沒官」為輕，詔八坐議。

translations.literal: At the time the officials considered the statute "For treason and rebellion, extending guilt to brothers by confiscating office" too lenient, and an edict ordered the Eight Dignitaries to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the officials considered the statute "For treason and rebellion, extending guilt to brothers by confiscating office" too lenient. An edict ordered the Eight Dignitaries to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 咸言漢、魏、晉謀反夷三族，請改從死。

translations.literal: All said that in Han, Wei, and Jin treason exterminated three clans; they requested changing to death.
translations.idiomatic: All said that in Han, Wei, and Jin, treason was punished by exterminating three clans, and they requested that the penalty be changed to death.

sentences.zh: 仁師曰：「父子天屬，足累其心，此而不恤，何愛兄弟？

translations.literal: Renshi said: "Father and son are bound by heaven—enough to weigh on the heart; if one does not care for this, how would one love brothers?"
translations.idiomatic: Renshi said: "Father and son are bound by heaven itself—enough to weigh on the heart. If the law does not care for that bond, how can it care for brothers?"

sentences.zh: 」房玄齡曰：「祖有廕孫義，則孫祖親重，而兄弟屬輕。

translations.literal: " Fang Xuanling said: "When the grandfather has the principle of shading the grandson, then the grandson-grandfather bond is heavy and the brother bond is light.
translations.idiomatic: " Fang Xuanling said: "When the grandfather has the principle of shading the grandson, the bond between grandson and grandfather is heavy and the bond between brothers is light.

sentences.zh: 今應重者流而輕者死，非用刑意。

translations.literal: Now what should be heavy is banished while what should be light is put to death—this is not the intent of punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Now what should be punished more heavily is merely banished, while what should be punished more lightly is put to death. That is not the intent of punishment."

sentences.zh: 」遂不改。

translations.literal: " The law was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The law was not changed.

sentences.zh: 後密請魏王為太子，失帝旨，左遷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Later he secretly petitioned that the Prince of Wei be made Crown Prince; he missed the emperor's intent and was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Later he secretly petitioned that the Prince of Wei be made Crown Prince. He missed the emperor's intent and was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 稍進民部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 及征遼東，副韋挺知海運，又別知河南漕事。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, he served as deputy to Wei Ting in overseeing sea transport, and separately supervised canal affairs in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Liaodong was launched, he served as deputy to Wei Ting in overseeing sea transport and separately supervised canal affairs in Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁師以漕路回遠，恐所輸不時至，以便宜發近海租賦餉軍。

translations.literal: Renshi, because the canal route was long and circuitous, feared supplies would not arrive in time, and on his own authority released nearby coastal rents and levies to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because the canal route was long and circuitous, Renshi feared that supplies would not arrive in time. On his own authority he released nearby coastal rents and levies to provision the army.

sentences.zh: 坐運卒亡命不以聞，除名。

translations.literal: He was punished because transport conscripts fled without his reporting it; his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished because transport conscripts fled without his reporting it, and his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 帝還至中山，起為中書舍人、檢校刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Zhongshan, he was reappointed Drafting Secretary and acting Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Zhongshan, he was reappointed drafting secretary and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 幸翠微宮，上《清暑賦》以諷。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Cuiwei Palace, he submitted "Rhapsody on Dispelling Summer Heat" as remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Cuiwei Palace, he submitted "Rhapsody on Dispelling Summer Heat" as a remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，賜帛五十段。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it and bestowed fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it and bestowed fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷中書侍郎，參知機務，被遇尤渥。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, participating in state affairs; the favor shown him was especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of the reign he was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat and participated in state affairs. The favor shown him was especially generous.

sentences.zh: 中書令褚遂良忌之，會有伏閤訴者，仁師不時上，帝大怒，流連州。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Chu Suiliang envied him; it happened that a petitioner at the palace gate complained; Renshi did not report it promptly; the emperor grew greatly angry and banished him to Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Chu Suiliang envied him. When a petitioner at the palace gate complained, Renshi did not report it promptly. The emperor grew greatly angry and banished him to Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，授簡州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was appointed Prefect of Jian and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he was appointed prefect of Jian Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 孫 湜

translations.literal: Grandson: Shi
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shi

sentences.zh: 子挹，挹子湜。

translations.literal: His son Yi; Yi's son Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi; Yi's son was Shi.

sentences.zh: 湜字澄瀾。

translations.literal: Shi, styled Chenglan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, styled Chenglan.

sentences.zh: 少以文詞稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was famed for his literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 第進士，擢累左補闕，稍遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was promoted successively to Left Supplementation Officer, and gradually transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, rose successively to left supplementation officer, and was gradually transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時桓彥范等當國，畏武三思槊構，引湜使陰汋其奸。

translations.literal: At the time Huan Yanfan and others held power; fearing Wu Sansi's fabricated accusations, they brought in Shi to secretly expose his treachery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huan Yanfan and others held power. Fearing Wu Sansi's fabricated accusations, they brought in Shi to secretly expose his treachery.

sentences.zh: 中宗稍疏功臣，三思日益寵，湜反以彥范等計告三思，驟遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhongzong gradually distanced the meritorious ministers; Sansi daily grew in favor; Shi instead reported Yanfan's plans to Sansi and was abruptly promoted to Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong gradually distanced the meritorious ministers, and Sansi daily grew in favor. Shi instead reported Yanfan's plans to Sansi and was abruptly promoted to drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 彥範等被徙，又說三思速殺之以絕人望。

translations.literal: When Yanfan and the others were transferred, he also urged Sansi to swiftly kill them to cut off popular hope.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanfan and the others were transferred, he also urged Sansi to kill them quickly so as to cut off popular hope.

sentences.zh: 三思問誰可使者，乃進其外兄周利貞。

translations.literal: When Sansi asked who could be sent, he recommended his maternal cousin Zhou Lizhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sansi asked who could be sent, Shi recommended his maternal cousin Zhou Lizhen.

sentences.zh: 利貞往，彥範等皆死。

translations.literal: Lizhen went; Yanfan and the others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen went, and Yanfan and the others all died.

sentences.zh: 擢利貞御史中丞。

translations.literal: Lizhen was promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Lizhen was promoted to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 湜附托昭容上官氏，數與宣淫於外。

translations.literal: Shi attached himself to Consort Shangguan of the Zhaorong rank and often openly committed lewd acts abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Shi attached himself to Consort Shangguan of the Zhaorong rank and often openly committed lewd acts outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，遷兵部侍郎，而挹為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War, while Yi was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of War, while Yi was vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武德以來，父子同為侍郎，惟挹、湜云。

translations.literal: Since Wude, father and son serving together as vice ministers—only Yi and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era, the only father and son to serve together as vice ministers were Yi and Shi.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書侍郎、檢校吏部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，與鄭愔同典選。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, acting Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and Associate Grand Councilor, and together with Zheng Yin jointly oversaw selection.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, acting vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and associate grand councilor, and together with Zheng Yin jointly oversaw official appointments.

sentences.zh: 納賂遺，銓品無序，為御史李尚隱劾奏，貶江州司馬。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes and gifts; ranks in selection were disorderly. Censor Li Shangyin impeached and memorialized against him, and he was demoted to Vice Military Administrator of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted bribes, and the ordering of candidates in selection fell into chaos. Censor Li Shangyin impeached him, and he was demoted to vice military administrator of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上官與安樂公主從中申護之，改襄州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangguan and Princess Anle interceded from within to protect him; [his punishment] was changed to Governor of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Shangguan and Princess Anle interceded on his behalf from within the palace, and his sentence was reduced to appointment as governor of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he entered [the capital] and became Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韋氏稱制，復以吏部侍郎同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan exercised regency, he was again made Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel with the rank of Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei held regency, he was again made vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and associate grand councilor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended, he was sent out as Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, Shi was sent out to serve as governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄除太子詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Steward of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，湜建言山南可引丹水通漕至商州，自商鑱山出石門，抵北藍田，可通挽道。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Shi proposed that in Shan'nan the Dan River could be diverted for grain transport to Shang Prefecture; from Shang one would cut through the mountain at the Stone Gate and reach northern Lantian, opening a tow-path.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shi proposed that water from the Dan River in the south could be diverted for grain transport as far as Shang Prefecture; from there a route could be cut through the mountains at the Stone Gate to northern Lantian, opening a tow-path.

sentences.zh: 中宗以湜充使，開大昌關，役徒數萬，死者十五。

translations.literal: Zhongzong made Shi commissioner, opened Dachang Pass, and employed laborers numbering in the tens of thousands; fifteen died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong appointed Shi commissioner and opened Dachang Pass, conscripting tens of thousands of laborers; fifteen men died.

sentences.zh: 禁舊道不得行，而新道為夏潦奔豗，數摧壓不通。

translations.literal: The old route was forbidden and could not be used, while the new route was battered by summer floods rushing and roaring, repeatedly wrecked and blocked so that it would not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Travel on the old route was forbidden, while the new route was repeatedly destroyed by summer floods and remained impassable.

sentences.zh: 至是論功，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At this time in reckoning merit he was granted Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, in accounting for his service, he was granted the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Glorious Culture.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，太平公主引為同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era, Princess Taiping brought him in as Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era, Princess Taiping had him appointed associate grand councilor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 進拜中書公。

translations.literal: He was further promoted and invested as Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時挹以戶部尚書得謝，而性貪，數為人請托以干湜。

translations.literal: At the time Yi, having been granted retirement as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was by nature greedy and often made requests on others' behalf to importune Shi.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yi had retired after serving as minister of the Ministry of Revenue; greedy by nature, he often solicited favors from Shi on others' behalf.

sentences.zh: 湜多不從，由是父子相失。

translations.literal: Shi mostly did not comply; from this father and son became estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Shi mostly refused, and from this the father and son fell out.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東宮，數至其第申款密。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, while in the Eastern Palace, often came to his residence to express warm intimacy in secret.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Xuanzong often visited Shi's home to confide in him in private.

sentences.zh: 湜陰附主，時人危之，為寒毛。

translations.literal: Shi secretly attached himself to the Princess; people of the time feared for him, and it made one's hair stand on end.
translations.idiomatic: Shi secretly cast his lot with Princess Taiping, and contemporaries feared for him; the very thought made one's hair stand on end.

sentences.zh: 門下客獻《海鷗賦》以諷，湜稱善而不自悛。

translations.literal: A client under his gate presented "Rhapsody on the Seagull" to satirize him; Shi praised it well but did not himself repent.
translations.idiomatic: A client presented "Rhapsody on the Seagull" as a satirical warning, but though Shi praised it, he did not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 帝將誅蕭至忠等，召湜示腹心。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to execute Xiao Zhizhong and others; he summoned Shi and showed him his inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to execute Xiao Zhizhong and the others, he summoned Shi and confided his plans to him.

sentences.zh: 弟澄諫曰：「上有所問，慎無隱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Cheng remonstrated, saying: "When the sovereign questions you, take care not to conceal anything."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Cheng remonstrated: "When His Majesty questions you, be careful not to conceal anything."

sentences.zh: 」湜不從。

translations.literal: Shi did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 及見，對問失旨。

translations.literal: When he was received, his answers in interrogation missed the sovereign's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned, his answers failed to satisfy the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至忠等誅，湜徙嶺外。

translations.literal: When Zhizhong and the others were executed, Shi was transferred beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhizhong and the others were executed, Shi was banished beyond the Ling mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 時雍州長史李晉亦坐誅，歎曰：「此本湜謀，今我死而湜生，何也？

translations.literal: At the time Li Jin, chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, was also condemned and executed; he sighed and said: "This was originally Shi's plot—now I die while Shi lives. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Jin, chief administrator of Yong Prefecture, was also executed; he sighed and said, "This plot was Shi's in the first place—why am I to die while he lives?"

sentences.zh: 」又宮人元稱嘗與湜謀進於帝。

translations.literal: Also the palace woman Yuan Cheng had once with Shi plotted to advance [their cause] before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: It also came out that the palace woman Yuan Cheng had once conspired with Shi to bring charges before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 追及荊州賜死，年四十三。

translations.literal: Pursued and caught at Jing Prefecture, he was granted death by imperial order; he was forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He was pursued and caught at Jing Prefecture, where he was ordered to take his own life; he was forty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 初，在襄州，與譙王數相問遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning, while at Xiang Prefecture, he and the Prince of Qiao often exchanged gifts and visits.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving at Xiang Prefecture, he and the Prince of Qiao often exchanged gifts and visits.

sentences.zh: 王敗，湜當死，賴劉幽求、張說護免。

translations.literal: When the prince was defeated, Shi was liable to death; he was spared thanks to Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue protecting and securing his release.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince fell, Shi was liable to execution, but Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue interceded and saved him.

sentences.zh: 及為宰相，陷幽求嶺表，密諷廣州都督周利貞殺之，不克。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, he entangled Youqiu in the region beyond the passes and secretly prompted the military commissioner of Guang Prefecture, Zhou Lizhen, to kill him; he did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chief minister, he contrived to send Youqiu to the far south and secretly urged Guang Prefecture military commissioner Zhou Lizhen to kill him—but the plot failed.

sentences.zh: 又與太平公主逐張說。

translations.literal: Again, together with Princess Taiping, he drove off Zhang Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Princess Taiping in driving Zhang Yue from office.

sentences.zh: 其猜毒詭險殆天性，雖蠆虺不若也。

translations.literal: His suspiciousness, venom, craftiness, and perilousness were almost inborn nature; even scorpion and viper could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: His suspicious cruelty and treacherous cunning were almost innate—even scorpions and vipers could not match him.

sentences.zh: 與弟液、澄、從兄涖並以文翰居要官。

translations.literal: With his younger brothers Ye and Cheng and his older male cousin of the same clan Li, all by literary talent held important offices.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brothers Ye and Cheng and his cousin Li all won important posts through their literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 每宴私，自比東晉王、謝。

translations.literal: At every private feast they compared themselves to the Wang and Xie of Eastern Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At private gatherings they likened themselves to the Wang and Xie clans of Eastern Jin.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾一門入仕，歷官未嘗不為第一。

translations.literal: He once said: "Our house entered office; in successive posts we were never other than first."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Every man of our house who entered office held the foremost rank at each step of his career."

sentences.zh: 丈夫當先據要路以制人，豈能默默受制於人哉！

translations.literal: A man ought first to seize the crucial road to control others—how can he silently be controlled by others!
translations.idiomatic: A man ought to seize the commanding position first and control others—how can he quietly submit to being controlled by others!

sentences.zh: 」故進趣不已，至於敗。

translations.literal: Therefore he pressed forward without cease, until ruin.
translations.idiomatic: And so he pressed ever forward until he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 湜執政時，年三十八，嘗暮出端門，緩轡諷詩。

translations.literal: When Shi held power he was thirty-eight; once at dusk he went out the Duan Gate, slackened reins, and recited poetry.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi was in power, at the age of thirty-eight, he once rode out at dusk through the Duan Gate, reins loose, reciting poetry.

sentences.zh: 張說見之，歎曰：「文與位固可致，其年不可及也。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yue saw this and sighed, saying: "Literary talent and rank can indeed be attained, but that age cannot be reached."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue saw him and sighed: "Literary talent and high office can indeed be attained—but not at that age."

sentences.zh: 孫 液

translations.literal: Grandson: Ye
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Ye

sentences.zh: 液字潤甫，尤工五言詩，湜歎，因字呼曰：「海子，我家龜龍也！

translations.literal: Ye, styled Runfu, was especially skilled in pentasyllabic poetry. Shi sighed in admiration and, using his style-name, called him: "Hai-zi—my family's tortoise and dragon!"
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Runfu, was especially accomplished in pentasyllabic verse. Shi marveled and, calling him by his style, cried, "Hai-zi—you are our family's treasure!"

sentences.zh: 」官至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His office reached Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of palace censor.

sentences.zh: 坐湜當流，亡命郢州，作《幽征賦》以見意，詞甚典麗。

translations.literal: Because of Shi's case he was liable to banishment; he fled as a fugitive to Ying Prefecture and wrote "Rhapsody on a Somber Journey" to express his mind—the language was very elegant and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in Shi's case, he was sentenced to banishment; he fled to Ying Prefecture and wrote "Rhapsody on a Somber Journey" to express his feelings in language of great classical beauty.

sentences.zh: 遇赦還，卒。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and returned; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and returned home, and later died.

sentences.zh: 子論，有吏幹，乾元中為州刺史，以治行稱。

translations.literal: His son Lun had administrative ability; in the Qianyuan era he served as prefect of a province and was famed for the quality of his governance.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun had real administrative talent; during the Qianyuan era he served as a prefect and was praised for the quality of his governance.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，遷同州刺史，為黜陟使庾何所按，議者不直何，故復用為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he was transferred to Tong Prefecture; he was investigated by the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Yu He; commentators did not uphold He's judgment, so Lun was again employed as Governor of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dali era he was transferred to Tong Prefecture, where he was investigated by the promotion-and-demotion commissioner Yu He; opinion held that He was in the wrong, and Lun was reappointed governor of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德宗以舊族耆年，擢大理卿，卒。

translations.literal: Dezong, because of his old family and venerable years, promoted him to Director of the Court of Judicial Review; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, honoring his old lineage and advanced age, promoted him to director of the Court of Judicial Review; he later died.

sentences.zh: 孫 澄

translations.literal: Grandson: Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Cheng

sentences.zh: 澄本名滌，玄宗改焉。

translations.literal: Cheng's original name was Di; Xuanzong changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's original name was Di; Emperor Xuanzong changed it for him.

sentences.zh: 帝在籓，與同里居。

translations.literal: When the emperor was in his fief, they lived in the same neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong was still a prince, they lived in the same neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 出潞州，賓友餞者止國門，而澄獨從至華。

translations.literal: When he left Lu Prefecture, friends and guests who saw him off stopped at the capital gate—but Cheng alone followed him as far as Hua.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince left Lu Prefecture, the friends who came to see him off stopped at the capital gate—but Cheng alone accompanied him all the way to Hua.

sentences.zh: 及即位，寵昵甚。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Cheng was favored and cherished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong took the throne, Cheng was greatly favored and indulged.

sentences.zh: 湜既誅，帝仍念之，用為秘書監。

translations.literal: Once Shi had been executed, the emperor still thought of Cheng and employed him as Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Shi was executed, the emperor still remembered Cheng fondly and appointed him director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，欲贈其父挹吏部尚書，宰相持不可，遂用四品禮葬，贈和州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, [Cheng] wished to posthumously grant his father Yi the title Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; the chief ministers held that this was impermissible, so a burial ceremony of the fourth rank was used instead, and Yi was posthumously granted Governor of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, Cheng wished to have his father Yi posthumously granted the title minister of the Ministry of Personnel; the chief ministers objected, so a fourth-rank funeral was performed instead and Yi was posthumously granted governor of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 澄侍左右，與諸王不讓席坐，性滑稽善辯，帝恐漏禁中語，以「慎密」字親署笏端。

translations.literal: Cheng attended at the emperor's side and did not yield seat or precedence to the princes; by nature he was witty and skilled in debate. The emperor feared he would leak palace talk, and personally wrote the characters "Be discreet" at the end of his court tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng attended the emperor's side and would not give way in seating even to the imperial princes; witty and quick with words, he so alarmed the emperor that Xuanzong personally inscribed the words "Be Discreet" on the end of his court tablet, fearing leaks of palace talk.

sentences.zh: 累遷金紫光祿大夫，封安喜縣子。

translations.literal: He was progressively transferred to Grand Master of Golden Purple and Glorious Culture, and enfeoffed as Baron of Anxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Grand Master of Golden Purple and Glorious Culture and enfeoffed as Baron of Anxi County.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted governor of Yan Prefecture.
